title: 🚗 Tesla to $500 in 2025: Why the Market May Be Underestimating This Next Leg
body:
Tesla ($TSLA) is poised to retest all-time highs and potentially hit $500 per share by the end of 2025. While many continue to debate valuation, several converging macro and micro catalysts suggest this move is not only possible—but increasingly probable.

⸻

🔋 1. AI & Full Self-Driving: Tesla’s Hidden Lever

Tesla is no longer just a car company. Its real long-term alpha may lie in its software margins from Full Self-Driving (FSD) and AI initiatives. With v12.4 rolling out and Dojo scaling up, Tesla could monetize autonomy at scale by late 2025, creating a high-margin SaaS-like layer that Wall Street hasn’t fully priced in.
	•	If FSD take rate increases from ~5% to even 20%, the profit boost is exponential.
	•	Dojo and Tesla Vision give them a vertically integrated edge no one else in the space has.

2. Energy Business Inflection Point

Tesla Energy (Megapack, Powerwall, virtual power plants) is quietly growing faster than the automotive segment. Energy storage deployments grew over 130% YoY, with margins climbing. As grid demand grows and battery storage becomes critical, Tesla is positioned to become a decentralized energy titan—with a $50B+ TAM in sight.

3. Global Expansion + Gen 3 Vehicle

The upcoming Gen 3 low-cost platform could be Tesla’s iPhone moment. Even if delayed to late 2025, a $25K vehicle would open untapped global markets (India, Latin America, Southeast Asia). Combined with Mexico and Berlin factory scaling, Tesla could unlock another 2–3M units/year in production capacity.

⸻

📈 4. Margin Expansion & Cost Control

Despite price cuts, Tesla has aggressively maintained industry-leading margins thanks to:
	•	Vertical integration (batteries, chips, software)
	•	OPEX discipline
	•	Simplified manufacturing (Giga press, unboxed assembly)

Q1 2025 could reflect normalization of margin pressure + tailwinds from robotaxi and energy.

⸻

💸 5. Valuation Compression + Sentiment Flip

Tesla currently trades at a forward P/E of ~60—down significantly from its highs. The market’s skepticism around growth and profitability could quickly reverse if one or more of these catalysts hit:
	•	Surprise energy revenue breakout
	•	FSD subscription adoption jump
	•	AI Day or Robotaxi reveal success
	•	Q3–Q4 delivery beats

Even a reversion to prior multiples could easily justify a $500 share price with modest earnings beats.

Final Thought

Tesla is trading like a car company with cyclical risks, but it’s morphing into a vertically integrated AI, robotics, and energy conglomerate. As that narrative returns to the forefront, $500 may be not a question of if, but when.

title: INTRODUCTION: Cathie Wood
body:
Let's be frank. While the hoi polloi might still be clutching their ARKK shares, anyone truly "in the know" has long since moved on, or at least, adjusted their gaze. Cathie Wood, bless her heart, certainly had her moment in the sun – a rather bright, fleeting supernova of speculative glory. But as the market matures and gravity reasserts itself, her particular brand of "disruptive innovation" looks less like prescience and more like… well, precisely what it is: a highly concentrated bet on unproven entities, fueled by an almost evangelical fervor.

To be seen still clinging to the ARK gospel is, frankly, a bit déclassé. One applauds the conviction, of course. It's almost quaint. But sustained wealth, the kind that truly matters, isn't built on chasing the latest shiny object, particularly when that object sheds value at a breathtaking pace. Those who mistake "big ideas" for actual profits often find themselves holding the bag, while the savvier among us quietly reallocate to more, shall we say, substantive opportunities.

So, as the market closes, consider this a gentle reminder: novelty fades. Performance, on the other hand, is eternal. And by that metric, dear Cathie, your time in the exclusive spotlight may well be, for the discerning investor, a relic of a bygone era. Good show, nonetheless.

Cathie Wood is a black widow spider that will crawl down the walls and eat ur portfolio young. And if she’s already losing, she will crawl right back and eat right back into it. She Carella Deville and she’s making waves again. 

God Bless you Cathie

title: 🚨 Red Flags About Top One Futures /OArmy Scam/@Neverpullover Scam
body:
1. Mailing Address in Wyoming
	•	Their listed address (1621 Central Ave, Suite 8433, Cheyenne, WY) is commonly used by registered agent and virtual mailbox services — meaning they may not have a real office there.
	•	Wyoming is a known state for businesses trying to avoid scrutiny, due to lax reporting rules.

2. No Clear Regulatory Oversight
	•	Despite offering futures trading access, they don’t appear to be registered with the CFTC or NFA — which are the official U.S. regulators for futures-related firms.
	•	If they’re not registered, they can’t legally offer real futures brokerage services to U.S. citizens — unless they’re a simulation-only prop firm, which should be clearly stated.

3. Changing Rules / Payout Disputes
	•	Some users on Reddit and QuantVPS report:
	•	Accounts being denied payouts
	•	Rules being enforced retroactively
	•	Disqualification for trades under 10 seconds (common in other shady prop firms too)
	•	These are classic signs of a “gotcha” funding challenge model: you pass, they find a reason to not pay.

title: The Stock Market …. When the Smoke Clears….
body:
So let’s break this down…

This administration answer :The jobs numbers were fake, we are firing the problem  

Not “oops we were off by a little.” No off by hundreds of thousands. May and June payrolls slashed. July wildly under expectations. Healthcare is carrying the job market like a body on its last leg. Manufacturing? Getting gutted.

And yet… stocks barely flinched?

This is where things get dangerous.

Because the market isn’t reacting to reality. It’s reacting to a fantasy that everything is fine, that a soft landing is still on the table, and that the Fed will somehow pull off the impossible: high rates, high inflation, slowing growth, and… no pain?

We’ve seen this movie before.

Back in 2007, everything looked “strong.” Home prices were “resilient.” Job market was “tight.” Economists were gaslighting everyone saying a recession was off the table. Lehman collapsed, and they still didn’t see it.

Then came the rug pull.

What we’re looking at now if these jobs revisions are real is not a “resilient” economy. It’s one being artificially held up by hope, corporate buybacks, and algorithmic fairy dust.

If you strip out healthcare the most subsidized sector in the economy we’ve been negative for 3 months straight. That’s recession territory. But they won’t call it a recession until it’s politically safe to do so. And by then? Too late.

And the market? It doesn’t care until it has to.

But when it has to, it doesn’t forgive.

We don’t know where the market goes from here. No one does. That’s the truth. But when price action diverges from fundamentals this hard it’s usually not “different this time.”

It’s the setup before the snap.

So yeah, maybe it rips higher. Maybe AI saves us. Maybe the Fed pulls a rabbit out of the hat. But if this house of cards falls  don’t say there weren’t signs.

The lies weren’t even hidden this time. They just hoped you weren’t paying attention.

title: Has anyone here dabbled in tax lien properties?
body:
Understand What a Tax Lien Is

When a property owner doesn’t pay their property taxes, the government can place a lien against the property. Instead of foreclosing, many counties sell that tax debt to investors via tax lien certificates.

You’re not buying the property you’re buying the right to collect the debt, often with interest (5%–36%).

⸻

Buy Tax Lien Certificates at Auction
	•	These auctions are held by counties check your county treasurer or tax collector’s website.
	•	You bid on tax liens (sometimes the interest rate, sometimes the premium).
	•	If you win, you pay the tax owed, and get a certificate with a repayment period (usually 1–3 years).

⸻

Earn Interest or Take Ownership
	•	If the owner pays the taxes back (which most do), you earn interest.
	•	If they don’t pay, after the redemption period, you may be able to:
	•	Foreclose on the property
	•	Apply for the deed 

This can result in you acquiring the property very cheap, though you’ll have to cover legal and foreclosure costs.

Any thoughts ?

title: PUBLIC NOTICE: The AfterHours Showdown
Paper Trading vs. Real Trading
body:
Paper Trading vs. Real Trading

Paper trading is like sitting in a Boeing 777 flight simulator. You can practice all the procedures, make perfect landings, and even “handle” emergencies. But there’s no real risk. Your palms don’t sweat, your stomach doesn’t drop when the market moves against you, and your decision-making isn’t under the same psychological load.

Live trading is like being in the actual cockpit of a 777, 35,000 feet in the air, with hundreds of passengers behind you and a storm ahead. Now it’s your money on the line. Every tick feels like turbulence, and hesitation costs you more than just points on a leaderboard.


The Miracle on the Hudson Parallel
In the US Airways Flight 1549 incident, Captain Sully Sullenberger landed an Airbus A320 on the Hudson River after both engines failed from a bird strike.

In simulations, many pilots failed the scenario not because they didn’t know the technical steps, but because simulations didn’t fully account for human factors: startle effect, uncertainty, environmental variables, and the weight of actual lives at stake.

Sully succeeded because of years of real-world flying experience dealing with real passengers, real emergencies, real weather, and the unteachable instinct that only comes from facing true risk.


The Core Point
Just like no simulator can perfectly replicate the adrenaline, fear, and decision-making pressure of an actual emergency landing…
No paper account can replicate the emotional swings, fear of loss, or greed of a real money trading 

You can know every chart pattern and trading strategy in “sim mode” but until you’ve felt your heart rate spike when your position drops $500 in seconds OR had to decide whether to cut or hold while the market rips you haven’t fully trained for the real thing.

Experience in live markets, like experience in live cockpits, builds instincts you can’t download or simulate.

Today was probably one of the most disappointing days on this app I’ve had in awhile…. You cannot defend the emotions behind a casino credit vs hard dead presidents. 

They smell completely different, and feel completely different. If I left my AMEX at a nice restaurant, and saw it was stolen and used, within minutes and a phone call I’m credited and a new card is FedEx overnighted the next day by 5:30 PM….. if shove 500 bucks in a money clip in 20s and get hammered golfing and I reach back in on hole 13th and slice a 20 off for Jamie’s tip for some double Tito’s and lose it somewhere hole 13 and the time I throw my golf bag in the car, guess who’s out 440 bucks and a sentimental money clip…. Me…..

title: The Whole Ball of Wax: How We Flip the Market Script
body:
Why this community really matters!

When people talk about markets, they often act like it’s some mysterious beast unpredictable, untamable, and only mastered by the suits on Wall Street. But here’s the truth: markets are nothing more than human behavior, scaled up. And when human behavior unites, it has weight. That’s where the “whole ball of wax” comes into play the idea that if a community acts with strategy, intention, and volume, it can shift outcomes in its favor.

1. Strength in Numbers

One person buying 10 shares is a drop in the ocean. A thousand people buying 10 shares each? Now we’re making waves. Collective buying power isn’t just about pushing price it’s about creating conviction. When a community moves together, it reduces hesitation, increases staying power, and builds resilience against fear.

2. Liquidity Becomes Leverage

Stocks move on supply and demand. When demand is organized, spikes aren’t random they’re engineered. Think of it like a group push: one person can’t shove a boulder, but if everyone leans in at the same time, momentum builds. A community that understands entry points, levels, and targets can create liquidity events in its favor.

3. Shared Intelligence, Shared Edge

The lone trader often makes emotional decisions. A collective, on the other hand, becomes a hive mind. Bad ideas get filtered out, stronger strategies rise to the top. Sharing knowledge, spotting setups, and calling out traps builds a sharper, faster, and more informed strategy than any one trader can develop on their own.

4. Psychology of Unity

The market thrives on manipulation institutions bet on fear, panic, and isolation. But when you know you’re not standing alone, the mental game changes. Selling too early feels less tempting. Holding conviction feels easier. The win doesn’t just belong to one person, it belongs to everyone who took the ride. That’s more powerful than chasing gains solo.

5. The Whole Ball of Wax

When the entire ball community, strategy, conviction, and execution rolls together, you don’t just play the game, you tilt the board. Collective buying isn’t about hype or blind faith, it’s about building a disciplined, profit-minded system where every individual benefits from the strength of the group.

At the end of the day, the market rewards those who play smart and play together. The lone wolf mentality might sound cool, but wolves hunt best in packs. And when the AfterHours community leans into that truth, the results aren’t random they’re inevitable

title: 🚩 Scammer Playbook on Telegram Trade Channels
body:
I asked Chat GPT about “Telegram Signal Artist” 

I ask you please like and share, and report over-posting. 
I’m starting to see the scum take on different users, and new fresh ideas to scam new folks. We are going into September, protect our community!

(What they do to lure people in)
	1.	Flashy Lifestyle Bait
	•	Post photos of Cars, Boats, piles of cash.
	•	Claim “all this came from my signals.”
	2.	Cherry-Picking & Deleting
	•	Delete bad trades, highlight wins only.
	•	Over time, their “win rate” looks unrealistically high (90%+).
	3.	Fake Screenshots
	•	Photoshop profits, or use demo accounts.
	•	Crop screenshots to hide trade size, broker, or timestamp.
	4.	Hindsight “Predictions”
	•	Say: “BTC will pump soon” or “SPY could crash.”
	•	After the move, they claim they called it.
	5.	Free Group Funnel → VIP Upsell
	•	Free channel = teasers, vague calls, hype.
	•	Losses in free group are spun into: “VIP members got the real call.”
	6.	Bot Inflated Memberships
	•	Buy fake followers so the group looks huge.
	•	“10,000+ members” but only a few likes/comments per post.
	7.	Fake Testimonials
	•	Post chat screenshots of “members” saying they made 300% in a day.
	•	Often these are sockpuppet accounts or bots.
	8.	Pressure Tactics
	•	“VIP spots closing tonight!”
	•	“Only 10 people left can join the inner circle.”
	•	Creates urgency to make you pay without thinking.

⸻

✅ How to Protect Yourself
	•	Never pay for signals without a verified audited track record (like Myfxbook or broker statements).
	•	Log their signals (like we covered earlier) — over time, you’ll see the truth.
	•	Beware of no-stop-loss trades — that’s how they fake big wins.
	•	Avoid lifestyle flexers — if someone’s legit, they don’t need to flaunt cars and watches to sell signals.

⸻

⚡Bottom line: Most Telegram trade groups are designed as scams from the start. Understanding their playbook keeps you safe — and if you track them, you can even expose their BS with hard data

🚩 Signs in Their Posting Behavior
	1.	Overposting / Spammy Volume
	•	Dozens of posts per day: signals, “market updates,” hype quotes, and testimonials.
	•	Purpose: overwhelm you so you don’t notice when calls contradict or fail.
	•	It creates a “buzz” effect even if the actual quality is garbage.
	2.	No Engagement (Likes/Reactions)
	•	Telegram channels can allow reactions 👍🔥😂, but many promoters don’t enable it — because low engagement would expose how few real members care.
	•	Or, if enabled, you’ll see 1–2 likes in a group of “10,000.” That’s a dead giveaway that the membership count is inflated with bots.
	3.	Constant Overhype
	•	Every trade is “the opportunity of the year.”
	•	Every market dip is “massive accumulation time.”
	•	Every minor win is “proof we’re unstoppable.”
	•	Over time, this boy-who-cried-wolf hype cycle makes users numb — until newbies show up and buy the pitch.
	4.	Copy-Paste Energy
	•	Messages often look templated:
	•	“🔥 NEW SIGNAL: BTC LONG 🚀”
	•	“VIP printing money 💰 join now!”
	•	Scammers recycle the same phrasing across multiple groups they run.

⸻

✅ What That Behavior Really Means
	•	Overposting = they’re trying to hide their bad calls in noise.
	•	No engagement = the group size is fake or people don’t trust them anymore.
	•	Overhype = they need new blood constantly, since old members lose money and leave.

So far two telegram guys who’ve blocked me for asking professional and simple questions.

title: Why Most Felons Can Only Use Robinhood ✅
body:
🚨 Why Many Felons Gravitate Toward Robinhood
	1.	Easiest Onboarding in the Industry
	•	Robinhood’s signup is app-based, instant, and asks very little beyond name, SSN, and address.
	•	Most legacy brokers (Fidelity, Schwab, etc.) have compliance screens that may flag felony convictions (especially fraud, financial crimes, or securities-related offenses).
	2.	No Human Gatekeepers
	•	Traditional firms often require manual review for flagged applicants.
	•	Robinhood’s process is automated — no branch manager or compliance officer is calling you up asking questions about your past.
	3.	No Licensing Needed
	•	Felons can’t become licensed financial professionals (FINRA bans them from holding Series 7, 63, etc., for at least 10 years, sometimes permanently).
	•	But to trade their own money, they don’t need a license — Robinhood makes that barrier almost invisible.
	4.	Accessibility
	•	Robinhood is built for retail traders with small amounts of capital.
	•	Other brokers may require higher minimum deposits or extra paperwork, while Robinhood lets you start with $1.
	5.	Perception in Online Communities
	•	Felons share in forums that other brokerages rejected them, while Robinhood accounts opened smoothly.
	•	This reputation snowballs: word spreads that “if you’ve got a record, Robinhood is your way in.”

⚠️ But Here’s the Flip Side
	•	Robinhood still reports to regulators — having a felony doesn’t exempt you from SEC/FINRA rules.
	•	Margin/Options can be limited if Robinhood’s risk models flag you.

title: Friends Making Money With Friends….
body:
AfterHours is built on friends, authenticity, and raw conversation. It’s messy, it’s real, it’s people calling things how they see it. You’ll never get that same energy in a corporate-controlled feed. Robinhood’s social layer will be heavily regulated, monitored, and designed to protect them not you. 

You won’t see NPOs running around the way you do here. 
You’ll see sanitized commentary, with compliance officers hovering over every post.

But here’s the kicker: when (not if) we move toward a 24-hour stock market (something Nasdaq has already piloted with overnight sessions since 2022), and when the $25,000 pattern day trading rule either gets rewritten or reinterpreted, the entire landscape will change. Social platforms attached directly to brokers like Robinhood’s will feel the weight of that change much more than underground communities like ours.

Examples:
	•	Nasdaq’s 24-hour futures pilot showed strong demand in the Asia-Pacific window. Imagine when retail has access around the clock. The pace of trading—and the pressure on traders will be unlike anything today.
	•	The SEC’s PDT rule (Rule 4210) has been in place since 2001. Robinhood will have to enforce it to the letter, while communities like AfterHours can actually talk strategy around it without fear of account flags.
	•	eToro and Public have tried social trading before, but always in a walled garden. You follow trades, sure but you never get authenticity. The risk-sharing and raw “callouts” culture? That lives here.

So yeah, Robinhood’s social might be flashy, and it’ll attract a crowd. But it will never feel like AfterHours. We’re not polished. We’re not regulated. We’re real. And when the market shifts into 24/7 mode, it’ll be communities like this one that actually set the tone.

AfterHours is where the soul of trading hangs out. Robinhood’s social? That’s just another platform.

🚨 Why You Don’t Sleep on AMEX Platinum & Gold if You Actually Have Money 🚨
body:
Listen if you’re broke, this convo ain’t even for you. But if you’ve got real cash flow, the AMEX Platinum & Gold aren’t “status cards,” they’re tools. Let me break it down:

1. The Fees Are Smoke & Mirrors.
Platinum looks like $695, Gold looks like $250. But if you cancel within 30 days of renewal, the fee is refunded. And before you cancel, you can negotiate — Amex doesn’t want to lose high-value cardholders. Retention offers are common: $150–$500 credits, or 30k–60k MR points (aka $450–$1,000+ in travel). That’s leverage.

2. The Credits Hedge the Cost.
Platinum stacks $200 airline incidental, $200 Uber, $240 digital entertainment, $189 CLEAR, $100 Saks, $300 Equinox, plus 5x points on flights. Gold throws $120 Uber, $120 dining, and 4x on restaurants/groceries. If you already spend in these lanes, you’re paying yourself back every month. It’s like prepaying your lifestyle and getting a rebate.

3. The Points Are Nuclear If You Know How to Play.
Chase portal? You get 1.5¢/point, nice and tidy. Amex transfer partners? You’re talking ANA biz class to Tokyo for 60k MR — a $7k ride. Virgin to Europe, Singapore Suites, Delta One redemptions… this is where points go from “cute” to generational leverage.

4. Negotiation Is the Hidden Game.
Amex values relationships. If you spend, pay on time, and threaten to cancel, they often throw offers at you to stay. Most people never even make the call. The smart ones do.

5. Why You Own Them If You Have Money.
Because wealth isn’t about pinching pennies, it’s about leverage. Platinum gets you airport lounges, hotel upgrades, automatic statuses, insane travel protections, concierge hooks. Gold feeds you 4x MR on everyday categories. Together? You’re hedging fees, compounding points, and creating optionality that poor thinkers never even see.

👉 Bottom line: If you’ve got money, not owning Platinum & Gold isn’t saving you anything — it’s costing you leverage, lifestyle, and points that multiply into real experiences. And if you ever feel the fee burn? Negotiate, downgrade, or cancel within the window. That’s not a loss — that’s playing chess.

💥 Own the cards. Use the credits. Negotiate the fees. Transfer the points. That’s how money works when you actually know what to do with it.

title: 🚨 The Real Wheel: Bank Account Edition 🚨
body:
Everyone talks about wheeling stocks, wheeling options, wheeling cars—cool. But the easiest money wheel you’re sleeping on? Bank sign-up bonuses.

Here’s the play:
	•	Banks are in a constant street fight for deposits.
	•	They dangle free money just to get you in the door—$200, $400, even $1,000+ for opening and dropping some cash for a few months.
	•	No charts, no Greeks, no guessing SPX levels. Just cold hard cash for letting your money sit still.

How to run the wheel:
	1.	Open a new account with a bonus offer. (Chase, Citi, PNC, Huntington, Wells, regional banks—you name it).
	2.	Meet the deposit or direct deposit requirements (usually just park $5k–$20k for 90 days, or reroute a paycheck).
	3.	Collect the bonus, wait out the terms, then withdraw.
	4.	Rinse, repeat, wheel into the next bank’s “free money” pot.

This is literally risk-free yield farming in the real world. No rug pulls, no rug burns—just banks begging you to borrow their credibility.

Example:
	•	Chase gives $600 for $15k parked 90 days. That’s basically a 16% annualized return on money that didn’t move.
	•	Do 2–3 of these per year, you’re pocketing an easy $1–2k on the side for letting your money breathe.
	•	Wheel it across different banks, stack bonuses, and laugh while everyone else is fighting Theta decay.

💡 Pro tip: Keep a spreadsheet. Track when you opened, when the bonus posts, and when you can close without a fee. It becomes a personal money-printing machine.

Most people won’t do it because it sounds “too easy.” That’s exactly why it works.

After Hours, remember: the real hustlers don’t just play markets. They wheel everything that pays.

💰 Be the bank’s worst nightmare. Be the guy that makes free money boring.

So here’s to Bobdog the legend, the blueprint, the reminder that life’s not about perfection, it’s about presence. Showing up, laughing when it hurts, and finding light in the storm.

If we all carried half of what Bobdog stood for loyalty, heart, quiet strength the world would look a little better after dark.

Be a little more Bobdog. 🐾

title: Enjoy the Getting Good While It’s Still Good…..
body:
Enjoy this while it lasts.
The opening bell. The closing bell. The silence in between. The rhythm that built traders, broke them, and built them again. 

Because make no mistake this is the last of the Mohicans.

Soon the market won’t sleep. 24/7 trading. AI flow. Crypto-style liquidity sloshing through weekends. No more “pre-market nerves” or “Friday fades.” Just an endless stream of algorithms and kids who’ve never known what it felt like to wait for 9:30.

Right now, we’re living in the last era where patience and timing mean something. Where human emotion still swings candles and not just code.

The pattern day trading rule? Outdated, soon to be rewritten by the same generation raised on instant dopamine and Trump-era volatility. These new players don’t care about cycles  they’ll rewrite them.

So while the getting’s good, enjoy the getting good.
Enjoy the panic, the euphoria, the 2:37 p.m. reversals that make no sense until they do. Because soon… this whole thing’s going full throttle, no brakes, no breaks.

We’re not just watching the market evolve we’re watching the end of the market as we know it.

title: Intrinsic Value Isn’t on a Chart …. It’s in the Pulse it’s… @SqueezeKid
body:
You can call a company trash. You can scream bearish till your lungs give out. You can throw every technical indicator, fib retracement, and Elliott Wave at the wall.

But at the end of the day it’s about intrinsic value.

Not the kind that lives in an earnings report or balance sheet. I’m talking about the real kind the heartbeat that moves people.

See, ORBS might be a lot of things. It might look like noise to the chart watchers, junk to the fund managers, or chaos to the risk managers. But intrinsic value in 2025 doesn’t live in spreadsheets anymore it lives on Twitter, AfterHours, and Discord. It spreads like energy. It builds, it hums, it creates FOMO.

Someone buys shares not because the RSI lined up, but because something inside them said, I just want to be a part of this.
And maybe they didn’t gain a lot. Maybe they didn’t lose a lot.
But someone else on the other side of that calls, puts, leverage, risk they felt it too.

That’s the beauty of this market.
It’s not just data it’s human emotion translated into price action.

I didn’t get RXRX at first. Or the kidz. Or why Squeeze was going nuclear hyped like a caffeine IV.
*But then I realized… he wasn’t just talking about a ticker. He was being himself.
And how can you fault that?
When something’s exciting, when it’s alive, when you’re the main cheer captain of a movement, that’s intrinsic value too*

It’s the human part of this whole mess the reason this market still moves.
Because once we stop moving and shaking… once the excitement fades… once the big players get swept out to sea and the rest of us stop believing in what we’re building together that’s when intrinsic value dies.

Until then, remember:
Charts fade. Plays expire. Hype cools.
But intrinsic value the real kind lives in the ones still showing up, still believing, still moving the needle.

*Because we are the intrinsic value*

I’ll play tummy sticks with you on this ORBS… @squeezekid but we’re gonna do it together. No vague bullshit. Transparency.

AI already knows your balance sheet, your habits, and whether your “money” smells real.
If you’re shopping online it’s quietly watching matching you to accounts, assets, debts and underwriting you in the background while you scroll.
I’ve been an underwriter long enough to tell fake money from the real shit at a glance. That sick little sense? It’s called experience underwriting for the modern age.
You think it’s anonymous. It isn’t. Welcome to the new front desk where AI fingerprints everything and decides who gets in and who stays out.


You don’t type a thing.
You pick your stuff, blink once, and it knows who you are.

The second you hit “Buy,” it’s already running a soft pull not a credit check, a life check.
Income verified. Debt cross-referenced. Risk tolerance mapped to every other purchase you’ve made since 2016.

Your last five grocery runs, your car’s mileage, that time you paused your insurance for “budgeting reasons” all of it quietly flows through a new underwriting layer.

And when it flashes “Approved ships tomorrow,” that’s not convenience.
That’s clearance.

Amazon doesn’t just sell you things anymore.

title: The Market Today was Planned and Well Orchestrated
body:
And Amazon was the scape goat. 

There was interest in SPY 550s…. 

	My Thesis ￼

1.	Positioning into key events – If there’s an upcoming Fed speech, earnings, or data release, large institutions often “pin” the market to certain levels to keep volatility contained. It’s like holding the ball in place before the kickoff.
	2.	Options market control – When there’s heavy open interest at specific strike prices (like SPY 550 calls or 545 puts), market makers hedge around those levels to stay delta-neutral. That creates a “magnet” effect, making the market grind or bounce predictably — it literally feels rigged because it’s being mechanically hedged.
	3.	Algorithmic balancing – High-frequency traders and systematic funds run models that rebalance off the same technical triggers (VWAP, moving averages, etc.), which can cause the market to move in lockstep. It gives that eerie “every candle is planned” feel.
	4.	Low volume, high control – On quieter days, fewer participants means the big players can move price with less resistance. It’s like they’re steering the ship while everyone else just watches.

title: Can you explain to me the correlation between slower markets and pink slips?
body:
1.	OTC “Pink Sheets” stocks 💹
	•	These are stocks traded over-the-counter (OTC) — not on major exchanges like the NYSE or NASDAQ.
	•	They’re called “pink slips” or “pink sheet stocks” because they were once literally listed on pink-colored paper distributed by the National Quotation Bureau.
	•	Usually:
	•	Very low-priced (often under $5/share — aka penny stocks).
	•	Lightly regulated, so financial info can be incomplete or unreliable.
	•	High risk, high reward, often used in pump-and-dump or speculative trading.

title: A Rendering Of Beyond Meat Holders for Monday!
A Take On Paid Discords/Scammers
body:
Why Good Paid Groups Actually Help
	

•	Skin in the Game: When people pay, they care. Free groups turn into noise. Paid ones usually attract traders who want to learn, not just screenshot.
	•	Accountability > Signals: A good community isn’t about hot picks it’s about process. It’s about learning why you lost, not pretending you didn’t.
	•	Tribe Energy: Trading solo can make you spiral. A real group gives you structure, people to compare notes with, and (hopefully) someone to talk you out of the next YOLO zero-day.

Why the Bad Ones Exist
	•	Fake Telegrams & WhatsApps: No real trader DMs you first. Ever. If someone slides in saying “Quick flip 5x guaranteed,” that’s a scammer with a $0 balance and 17 stolen profile pics.
	•	Fake Influencers: Check for consistent posting and real conversation. If the account only posts screenshots of wins or calls themselves a “market wizard,” it’s cosplay.
	•	Paywalls for Chaos: If the group looks more like a frat house than a focus group, you’re paying rent on noise.


• People pay ……people care.
• Structure beats chaos.
• Real traders teach process, not pump dreams.
• You get a tribe ……. and a reality check.


Now, if you have a discord, I’d like you to introduce yourself, and a link…. And tell us why a discord like yours works, and what you do to set yourself a-part . I kindly ask everyone is professional.

⚠️ Inside the mind of the Telegram Scammer
body:
For anyone new, or for anyone who is having trouble navigating AfterHours. You’ll find eventually that you stumble around and figure out profiles.  Then you figure out there are links, these links lead to discords or… my personal favorite telegrams. 

I am going to give you a play by play about how these scams work. Step one, you download an unregulated app from overseas that has no laws or any support protecting you from the scammer. They can take your information and use plays against you. You’ll find the accounts are often riddled with stolen pictures, fake cars they pretend to have, and in order to “get more premium access” you pay money. 

@444Stock this was from inside your telegram you started October 1st. (He wants paid now for plays) he sucked everyone in …. And now wants 150.00 a month 

Is this who you want giving you “plays”
When they rip pictures off the internet from Instagram and claim those as their own? 

All it takes a handful of these telegram scammers to connect (and they all do) and shout to buy 10 contracts of QQQ…. And they do calls when they told the group
To do puts…. 

So think about it, 5-7 telegrams 
400 stupid people….  

If he’s ripping pictures off the internet, and isn’t being legit, and collecting money from you from Cash App, PayPal, you name it, he’s being a shade ball…. Everyone will lash out and say “oh what happened”

And one day, after losing money…. The telegram folds up, or changes names, or keeps the same AfterHour tips, and it rebrands itself….. 

Do me a solid favor, go to @444stock, maybe download telegram, research it. If you feel generous leave him a tip directly on his profile …. Getting the message out to people that they are being swindled is important.

title: The Epstein Files are released
It’s wild how life can change in an instant….
body:
One minute you’re coasting through routine check-ups, thinking it’s just another box to check. Then suddenly that “routine scan” turns into a PET scan on Monday… a consultation on Tuesday… and tomorrow, a bronchoscopy that might be one of the most significant moments of my entire life.

I won’t pretend I’m not scared. I am. I’m young, and I thought I had more time before facing anything like this. But life doesn’t always give warnings. It just shows you what truly matters.

And right now, all the noise the markets, the charts, the trade took a backseat real fast. When you’re staring at something bigger than yourself, you realize how small the things you once obsessed over really are. Perspective hits different when your health becomes the center of the universe.

But even in the middle of this storm, there’s grace. Real grace. The kind that slows you down, softens you, makes you more aware of the good people around you. It makes you want to try harder to be kinder gentler, more patient, more present. We don’t get to choose every chapter, but we do get to choose how we show up in the hard ones.

And to everyone on AfterHour. ….. thank you. Thanks for letting me be part of your journey, and for being part of mine. Hold tight to what matters. And yeah… stay on top of these scammer dirtbags while I handle my own battle. Life’s too short to let clowns run wild.

Whatever comes next I’m facing il face it head on With clarity… With fight. With gratitude.

Here’s to grace and perspective, and to the people who make the journey worth it.

All of you are so very special to me In so many ways, I will continue to be apart of this community, I just need to take a step back for what is really important.

title: Who WOULDN’T you trust managing your money?
The Picture We Never Talk About: Lifetouch, Shutterfly, Big Finance… and the Data Trail No One Sees
body:
My Thanksgiving Conversations…. 
My family is comprised of journalist, and government…. And I am sprinkled in. 

*** I asked for Chat GPTS help writing this article***** 
Because it’s a lot to take in….. 

Here we go …..  

Every parent knows the drill.
Picture Day comes, kids line up, Lifetouch snaps a few photos, and a few weeks later the envelopes or links arrive. Cute, simple, harmless.

But what most people never think about is this:

You’re not just buying a photo.
You’re entering your kid into a data pipeline.

And the biggest players behind that pipeline aren’t photographers…
They’re investment giants like BlackRock, Vanguard, and tech companies whose entire business is built on analyzing and monetizing data.

Let’s break down the web.

⸻

1. Lifetouch → Shutterfly → Big Data Ownership

Lifetouch used to be a standalone photography company.

Then Shutterfly bought them.

Then Shutterfly itself got scooped up by private equity and sits in a network of major institutional investors—firms like BlackRock and Vanguard, the same names that show up behind half of corporate America.

When you combine school photos + cloud storage + massive investment firms, you get something way bigger than yearbook nostalgia:

a proprietary archive of millions of children’s faces, birthdays, locations, and school info—indexed and stored for decades.

That’s not photography.
That’s a dataset.

⸻

2. When Data Becomes a Product

Here’s where things get uncomfortable.
	•	Faces
	•	Heights
	•	Ages
	•	Locations
	•	Names
	•	School districts
	•	Family purchase patterns

This isn’t “just pictures.”
It’s a blueprint for future ad targeting, consumer profiling, and predictive analytics.

And the money behind it is the same money behind every other large-scale data capture system in the country.

⸻

3. Where PLTR (Palantir) Enters the Conversation

To be crystal clear:
There is no public evidence that Palantir touches Shutterfly or Lifetouch data.

But the conversation gets interesting because:
	•	Palantir specializes in AI-driven identity recognition
	•	They build tools for government and security agencies
	•	Their tech is built to ingest massive visual datasets
	•	Schools and law enforcement increasingly use tech platforms for safety and monitoring

So when people ask,
“What happens to millions of children’s photos stored by a giant data company?”

The fear isn’t about what is happening.
It’s about what could happen in the future—especially as AI becomes able to link faces, locations, and real-world movement at scale.

⸻

4. Drones, Cameras, and the Future of Tracking

Connect this with the rise of:
	•	autonomous drones
	•	school security systems
	•	facial recognition algorithms
	•	AI surveillance tools
	•	real-time tracking systems

Suddenly the idea of large, clean, labeled photo databases of children doesn’t feel so innocent.

If a growing surveillance ecosystem needs faces to train on…
Where do you think those datasets come from?

Everything is “anonymous,” until it isn’t.

⸻

5. Follow the Money

Here’s the part nobody likes to talk about:

Data is worth more than the picture orders.
Way more.

Photos used to be a product.
Now photos are the raw material.

When companies are backed by trillion-dollar asset managers like BlackRock and Vanguard, their incentives shift:

Not “take pictures.”
But capture data. Store data. Monetize the pipeline.

The photos aren’t the business.
The information is.

⸻

6. Why People Are Spooked

It isn’t that Lifetouch or Shutterfly are doing anything illegal.

It’s that we now live in a world where:
	•	every app wants your face
	•	every company wants your data
	•	every platform uses AI to train on images
	•	every investment group chases long-term data assets
	•	every technological system is moving toward surveillance-style automation

Put all of it together, and picture day looks… different.

⸻

7. Maybe the Scariest Part: Nobody Reads the Fine Print

Parents click:

“✔ I agree.”

Kids smile.

Cameras flash.

And somewhere, that image—your child at age 7, 8, 9—sits in a data center owned by a company owned by an investment giant whose entire portfolio is built around scaling information.

Photos disappear from your fridge.

But they never disappear from the cloud.

title: 🚨 PUBLIC SERVICE ANNOUNCEMENT: WORDS LIKE “PARTNERSHIP” HAVE LEGAL CONSEQUENCES 🚨
body:
PART 2: 

https://afterhour.com/Freeballer/bbxn/part-2-of-tell-me-lies-tell-me


cs@us.moomoo.com

 1-888-721-0610(English) 1-888-721-0660(Chinese)

1️⃣ “Partnership” is a legally defined business relationship.

Under U.S. law (including Uniform Partnership Act standards), the term “partnership” implies:
	•	mutual consent between both parties
	•	shared liability
	•	shared profits and losses
	•	formal contractual agreement

You cannot call yourself a partner of a company without the company’s explicit authorization.

Doing so is considered false representation.

⸻

2️⃣ Moomoo’s own Terms make it very clear.

Directly from their Terms of Use:

“This Agreement does not create any partnership, joint venture, employer-employee, agency or franchisor-franchisee relationship between you and Moomoo.”

Source: https://www.moomoo.com/terms

This is legally binding.

Meaning:
🚫 You cannot imply Moomoo endorses you.
🚫 You cannot imply you represent Moomoo.
🚫 You cannot claim you’re in a partnership with them.

⸻

3️⃣ Misusing the word “partnership” in finance creates regulatory problems.

Falsely claiming a partnership with a regulated broker can fall under:

• False Endorsement

Claiming association with a company without permission.

• Misrepresentation

Providing misleading claims that could influence consumer behavior.

• Unfair or Deceptive Acts or Practices (UDAP)

Federal and state consumer protection laws prohibit misleading financial claims.

• Inducement

Encouraging people to take action based on a fabricated or unverified relationship.
This is extremely sensitive in the world of trading, recruiting, and finance.

• FINRA Advertising Rule 2210 violations

Regulated brokers must maintain strict control over who claims affiliation with them.

If someone is publicly implying an endorsement by or partnership with a licensed brokerage — without documentation — that can be interpreted as unauthorized promotion.

⸻

4️⃣ No press release = no partnership.

Every legitimate partnership with a brokerage is:
	•	announced
	•	documented
	•	press-released
	•	publicly verifiable

If Moomoo hasn’t said it, it doesn’t exist.

And in this case?

Moomoo has said absolutely nothing.

⸻

5️⃣ Final Verdict

Anyone publicly claiming:

“We officially partnered with Moomoo”

without a contract, approval, or announcement…

…is engaging in unauthorized representation, misleading endorsement, and false use of partnership terminology.

Legally, financially, and ethically?

It’s not just wrong — it’s prohibited.

And Moomoo’s own Terms prove it.

📎 Source: https://www.moomoo.com/terms
📎 “No partnership or agency relationship is created.”

title: Squeeze Kids Poll: Not Mine
body:
How Pump & Dumps Are Usually “Devised”

A classic pump-and-dump has three coordinated pieces:

1. Narrative Pump

Someone (or a group) builds hype:
	•	“Curtain call!”
	•	“Next leg incoming!”
	•	“Load before the PR drops!”
	•	Claims of shorts covering, magical catalysts, or “MM manipulation.”

This is usually done in:
	•	Discords
	•	Twitter/X
	•	Reddit
	•	Group chats
	•	Private DMs

The point is to attract liquidity — get outsiders to buy.

2. Silent Accumulation → Silent Offloading

The people running the hype do not trade the way they tell others to.

Before the pump:
	•	They quietly accumulate shares or call options.

During the pump:
	•	They sell into the very retail buying they created.

This creates the illusion of bullish momentum… right before they dump into it.

3. The Hidden Move: “Buying Against the Other Way”

You mentioned:

“when you tell people to buy a curtain call but it is bought against the other way with more money”

That’s exactly how these schemes work.
Here’s what that means operationally:
	•	They hype BUY BUY BUY publicly.
	•	Meanwhile, in their real account, they are:
	•	Selling shares into your buying
OR
	•	Opening big short positions (puts or short stock)
	•	OR hedging via OTM options that profit if price collapses

Because they have more capital, their hidden trades outweigh the retail hype buying.
That’s why the chart looks like:
	1.	Sudden spike (the pump)
	2.	Immediate violent drop (the dump)

The insiders profit massively by selling high or shorting high.

⸻

Why the Pump Works Even If They’re Selling

Because retail buyers react to green candles, not fundamentals.

If they can push price up briefly, retail FOMO rushes in:
	•	Everyone buys on momentum
	•	Volume spikes
	•	Liquidity rises
	•	Insiders offload their position instantly

Retail → buys the top
Operators → sell into retail liquidity
Chart → rug pulls

⸻

How a Group Pulls This Off Without Being Caught

Coordination + stealth.

They don’t say “Let’s manipulate this” — that’s illegal and stupid.
Instead they use coded language:
	•	“Curtain call”
	•	“Ring the bell”
	•	“She’s about to go”
	•	“MMs suppressing it”
	•	“They’re loading under the surface”
	•	“Someone knows something”

And they never say they’re selling — they simply do it.

Because it’s:
	•	Small cap
	•	Low float
	•	Thin liquidity

…large coordinated orders can move it dramatically.

⸻

Why the Chart Looks Rigged

Because small-cap pumps usually are.

What you described —
“Tell people to buy it, but insiders buy against the other way with more money” —
is literally the textbook playbook.

Retail sees:
	•	A spike
	•	A big green bar
	•	Twitter hype
	•	Fake volume

Meanwhile, insiders are:
	•	Exiting
	•	Shorting
	•	Dumping inventory

When they’re finished, liquidity dries up instantly, and the price collapses.

3. Learned Helplessness
	•	He has trained himself to believe:
“Why work when someone else will pay me? It’s easier to stay stuck.”
	•	This becomes a mental trap, where he believes helplessness is his identity.

⸻

4. Zero Accountability
	•	“I can’t feed my dog”
	•	“I have to pay someone to watch it”
	•	“I can’t get a job”

Every sentence is an external excuse, not an internal solution. No accountability = no change.

⸻

5. Financial Irresponsibility
	•	Can’t feed a dog…
	•	But can pay someone to “watch it”?
	•	That’s upside-down logic, which signals someone who is either lying or financially incompetent.

⸻

6. Self-Inflicted Crisis
	•	He CHOOSES not to work.
	•	Gas stations, warehouses, fast-food, labor gigs, temp agencies—all hiring.
	•	He is manufacturing his own emergency to justify begging.

⸻

7. Avoidance of Real Help

He refuses:
	•	Job programs
	•	Employment centers
	•	Shelters
	•	Food banks
	•	Animal rescues
	•	Assistance programs

People who truly need help go where help is given.
People who want to avoid structure choose the streets.

⸻

8. Exploitation Psychology

He’s not begging—he’s running a low-effort emotional con:
	•	No overhead
	•	No schedule
	•	No rules
	•	No accountability

He preys on compassionate people because he knows empathy is profitable.

⸻

9. Victim Identity Addiction

His entire identity becomes:
“Poor me. I’m the guy who can’t feed his dog.”
He gets:
	•	attention
	•	sympathy
	•	money
	•	validation
	•	a sense of purpose

If he got a job, he’d lose the identity he’s built his self-worth around.

⸻

10. The “Dog Shield” Tactic

People won’t question him because:
	•	“At least he’s trying to help his dog.”
	•	“The dog didn’t choose this.”

The dog becomes a human shield protecting him from criticism.

⸻

11. Dependency Loop

By giving him money:
	•	You reinforce the behavior.
	•	He learns the streets pay better than work.
	•	The cycle continues.
This is behavioral conditioning—like rewarding a bad habit.

⸻

12. Zero Effort to Improve

He could:
	•	Sweep floors
	•	Pump gas
	•	Do dishwashing
	•	Do day labor
	•	Stock shelves
	•	Work overnight shifts
	•	Work temp agencies

Even the bare minimum job would out-earn panhandling.
But he refuses effort, which shows preference, not inability.

⸻

13. Exploiting the Dog’s Welfare

If he truly couldn’t care for the dog:
	•	He’d surrender it
	•	Or find a rescue
	•	Or let a shelter place it
	•	Or let someone foster it

But he keeps the dog because it’s part of the empathy machine.

⸻

14. Manipulating Empathic People

People who care, give.
People who care, also feel guilty saying no.
He knows this.
It’s a psychological trap that punishes compassion.

⸻

15. Twisted Priorities

“Paying someone to watch the dog”
instead of
“getting a job to care for the dog”

This is a mental disconnect—illogical thinking, often tied to:
	•	avoidance
	•	immaturity
	•	entitlement
	•	laziness
	•	manipulation

⸻

16. Entitlement Mindset

He believes:
	•	The world owes him
	•	Strangers owe him
	•	Society owes him
	•	People with money owe him

But he owes nothing back.
That’s toxic entitlement.

⸻

17. No Intention to Change

People stuck in genuine hardship WANT change.
He wants comfort without effort.
He doesn’t want a ladder out—he wants padding at the bottom.

⸻

18. Unhealthy Social Reinforcement

He gets:
	•	Conversation
	•	Attention
	•	Sympathy
	•	Drama
	•	Money
	•	Validation

Begging becomes social income, not financial income.

⸻

19. Transfer of Responsibility

By asking others to feed his dog, he is effectively saying:
“YOU take responsibility for MY choices.”
That is manipulative and irresponsible.

⸻

20. Emotional Parasite Behavior

He draws energy, emotion, pity, and resources from other people.
That’s called emotional parasitism—relying on others’ guilt as fuel.

⸻

21. False Narrative Building

“I pay someone to watch the dog”
is likely:
	•	an excuse
	•	a deflection
	•	or a partial lie

Manipulative people use messy stories to avoid deeper questions.

⸻

22. He’s Not Motivated Because People Keep Saving Him

Every dollar handed to him is a message:
“Keep doing this.”

⸻

23. Victim-Centered Morality

He’s convinced that because he’s “struggling,” ethics don’t apply to him:
	•	lying
	•	manipulating
	•	coercing
	•	exploiting sympathy

All becomes “okay” because he’s struggling. That’s warped thinking.

⸻

24. He’s Using People Who Genuinely Want to Help

Good people think they’re helping the dog.
He’s helping himself.
And not in a good way.

⸻

25. Long-Term Harm

You’re not helping him:
	•	grow
	•	mature
	•	take responsibility
	•	get stable
	•	become independent

You’re enabling the very behavior that keeps him stuck.




Edit :
Supporting him hurts him, hurts the dog, and rewards manipulation.
There is nothing morally or psychologically healthy about enabling a capable adult who refuses to work but uses an animal as a prop to extract sympathy from strangers.

Here’s my dream: for 2026, I want to know who’s starting a fucking business, I want you to remember this post….

The government does not fund vibes, dreams, or “I’m thinking about…”

They fund activity.

So if your sentence starts with:

“One day I want to start a business…”

You get nothing.

If it starts with:

“I have a business and need help executing…”

Now you’re in the game.


Step 1: Stop Trying to Be Fancy

You don’t need:
	•	An office
	•	A logo
	•	A website
	•	A truck
	•	A loan

You need:
A business category
Paperwork
Motions
Repeat


Pick something boring and legal:
	•	Consulting
	•	Services
	•	Digital work
	•	Training
	•	Mobile services

Boring gets funded.
“Revolutionary ideas” get ignored.


Step 2: Form the LLC (This Is the Key)

An LLC is the entry ticket.

No LLC = no help
No EIN = no conversation
No paperwork = no money


And if you truly don’t have the filing fee, guess what?

The government will pay for it… if you ask.

That’s how stupid this system is.


Step 3: Walk Into the Free Help Buildings

Yes. Buildings. With people. Who get paid whether you win or lose.

Small Business Development Center (SBDC)

This is the cheat code nobody uses.

They:
	•	Build your business plan
	•	Help you apply for grants
	•	Find startup money
	•	Do the forms with you

For free.

Say this exact sentence:

“I’m starting a business with limited capital and need help accessing grants, reimbursements, or no-cost startup programs.”

Do not freestyle. Say that.



Step 4: Start Doing Something

This part separates the adults from the crybabies.

You must:
	•	Send invoices
	•	Track mileage
	•	Save receipts
	•	Spend time learning
	•	Make attempts

No activity = no funding
Motion unlocks money.



Step 5: Use Soft Money First

Not loans. Not debt. Not stress.

Soft money means:
	•	Reimbursements
	•	Training grants
	•	Wage subsidies
	•	Equipment credits
	•	Fee waivers

You spend → they pay you back.

That’s how you survive without capital.


Step 6: Loans Are LAST

If you go straight to loans, you already lost.

Loans come after:
✔ Structure
✔ History
✔ Proof of effort

Microloans exist for broke starters, but only if you did the steps above.


The Part Nobody Wants to Hear

This system rewards:
	•	People who show up
	•	People who fill out forms
	•	People who follow instructions
	•	People who don’t quit when it’s boring

It does not reward:
	•	Complaining
	•	Waiting
	•	“I’m stuck”
	•	“They should help me”



Freeballer ♥️ 

You don’t need money.
You need paperwork + motion.

title: Part II: How to Trade $SPY
body:
Let’s talk about SPY, volume, and how this quiet, polite-looking market eats premium and hurts profits while pretending everything is “fine.”

Here’s the uncomfortable truth:

When volume is low, SPY doesn’t need to wreck you with a crash.
It doesn’t need to reward you with a trend.
It just needs to hover.

And while it hovers your options premium is getting chewed up.

Low-volume SPY is a premium decay factory.

No follow-through.
No urgency.
No institutions pressing size.

You get:
• Fake breakouts
• Micro pumps
• Soft sell-offs
• Endless chop around key levels

You buy calls SPY goes up 40–60 cents, stalls, IV cools, theta kicks in.
You buy puts SPY drops a buck, volume disappears, bounce comes, premium dies.

That’s not trading — that’s being slowly taxed.

Now here’s the part people miss 👇

⚠️ Low volume actually makes SCALPING easier if you know what you’re doing. ⚠️ 

Why?
Because:
• Levels respect better
• Moves are smaller and cleaner
• Algos pin price
• Mean reversion works

Scalpers can take:
• Quick 20–40 cent SPY moves
• Fast in / fast out contracts
• No hope, no hold, no hero trades

But the moment you try to swing in low volume?
You’re donating premium.

Freeballer rules:
Low volume = bad for swings
Low volume = good for disciplined scalps

Hold time is the real enemy
This is where traders get hurt:
They see a level break.
They assume continuation.
They hold.
Volume never comes.
Theta does the rest.

Smart money waits for volume confirmation.
How I adapt adapt…
Size down
 Shorten timeframes
Take profits faster
Walk away sooner

If volume isn’t there, SPY isn’t “setting up” 
it’s setting a trap.

Call it what it is.
Trade what’s in front of you.
Protect your premium.

Freeballer 💥

title: Part III: How to Own a Business for Tax Reasons ….
body:
Alright, I’m gonna say this clean enough to stay legal, but raw enough to be real because there’s a difference between tax evasion (stupid, illegal, orange jumpsuit) and tax manipulation (legal, boring, IRS-approved, rich people do it every day).

This is Freeballer math, not TurboTax fairy tales.

Owning a Business Is Free Money (If You Stop Thinking Like an Employee)

W-2 brains get taxed first, then they try to survive on what’s left.

Business owners?
We get taxed last after we decide what profit even means.

That’s the game. That’s the cheat code. That’s the part nobody explains because if they did, people would stop worshipping overtime.

Tax Brackets Are a Psychological Weapon

Here’s the lie:

“If you make more money, you get taxed more.”

Wrong.

You only get taxed more if you show more taxable income.

Employees can’t hide.
Business owners can rearrange reality.

Revenue …. income
Income ….. taxable income
Taxable income ….cash in your pocket

If you don’t understand that sentence, you’re paying retail on life.

Employees Pay Taxes on GROSS. Owners Pay on WHAT’S LEFT.

Employee:
	•	Earn $100k
	•	IRS takes its bite immediately
	•	You argue with yourself over Starbucks

Business owner:
	•	Bring in $100k
	•	Run it through the business
	•	Decide what’s expense, what’s reinvestment, what’s timing
	•	IRS sees what you allow them to see

Same money.
Different outcomes.
One of you is broke and angry online

The “Manipulation” (Legal, Boring, Devastatingly Effective)

Let’s be honest — the system was built for owners, not workers.

Here’s how the manipulation actually works:

• You delay income
• You accelerate expenses
• You depreciate assets
• You expense your life (within reason, calm down)
• You control timing, which controls brackets

The IRS doesn’t ask:

“Did you work hard?”

They ask:

“What’s your taxable income?”

And that number is negotiable.

Final Freeballer Truth

Owning a business isn’t about hustling harder.
It’s about deciding when, where, and if you pay taxes.

I’m not hiding money.
I’m moving it.

I’m not broke.
I’m optimized.

And once you see it, you can’t unsee it.

Employees ask:

“How much do I make?”

Owners ask:

“How much do I show?”

That’s the whole game.

title: Part IV: Getting Off You’re ass and starting you’re own Tax Haven/Business
body:
This is the best month to start a business…. 
Gives you something to do in January and February and March….. 


You’re tired?
Good.
That means you’re awake.

Because here’s the truth nobody likes admitting:

If you don’t own something, you are something being owned.

Your alarm clock isn’t neutral.
Your paycheck isn’t security.
Your job doesn’t “take care of you.”
It rents you by the hour and drops you the second the math changes.

And you keep saying:

“I’ll start when I have time.”
“I’ll start when I have money.”
“I’ll start when I feel ready.”

The reality : I’m comfortable being uncomfortable.

Starting a business isn’t glamorous.
It’s not coffee shop vibes and passive income reels.

The Real Minimum (Reality Check)

You don’t need “startup capital.”
You need friction money just enough to remove excuses.

Absolute bare minimum:

$100–$500

That’s it.
Not to build an empire to start.

If you can’t start with that, money isn’t the problem. Execution is.


What That Money Actually Covers

Tier 1: Survival Mode Startup ($100–$250ish) depending on state 

This is “I’m serious but not stupid.”
Business registration (LLC or sole prop): $50–$150 (state dependent)
Domain name: $10–$15
Basic tools (email, software, subscriptions): $20–$50

No office.
No logo agency.
No business cards you’ll lose in 48 hours.


Tier 2: Functional Business ($250–$500ish) 

Now you’re operational, not pretending
Everything aboutBasic website or landing page: $50–$150
Accounting software or spreadsheet system: $0–$30
Small buffer for ads, samples, or outreach: $50–$100

This is enough to:
Invoice
Collect money
track expenses
Look legitimate


What You Don’t Need (But People Waste Money On)

Office space
Fancy logo
Business coach
Paid ads on day one
“Scaling tools” for zero revenue
A $5,000 website nobody visits

If your business can’t make money without these, it won’t make money with them.



The Dirty Truth

Most real businesses start with:
A skill
A phone
A problem someone will pay to solve

title: 🚨 AFTERHOURS ALERT: KNOW THE RED FLAGS 🚨 NEW FOLKS 🚨
body:
Listen up, new people this is your survival guide for navigating AfterHours. Not everyone here is playing fair. Some are out to scam, manipulate, or waste your time. If you spot these signs, stay away:

1️⃣ Promises that sound too good to be true
Free money, “secret” plays, guaranteed wins if it’s that perfect, it’s a trap. Nothing is guaranteed, and anyone pushing it is hunting for a quick scam.

2️⃣ Pressure & urgency
“Do this now or miss out.” Real people don’t rush you to make moves. If someone is aggressive with timelines, it’s a major red flag.

3️⃣ Evasive answers
Ask questions, and they dodge, change the topic, or get defensive. Transparency is everything if they can’t give it, walk.

4️⃣ Requesting private info or money first
Account info, login credentials, wire transfers, crypto wallets any of it. NEVER share it. That’s how scams start.

5️⃣ Fake verification & screenshots
People will try to flex with fake wins, screenshots, or cloned profiles. Learn to spot the fakes look for inconsistencies, editing, or impossible numbers.

6️⃣ Too flashy, too polished
Over-the-top stories, luxury pics, big claims this is often a mask for someone not to be trusted.

⚡ Pro tip: Trust your gut. If it feels off, it probably is. AfterHours is a community, but it’s also a jungle. Protect your account, your info, and your wallet.

💥 Rule of thumb: If someone ticks two or more of these boxes, cut them off immediately. Don’t debate just move on.

Remember: the game here is awareness. Stay sharp, play smart, and don’t let the scammers win

Watch out for fake tips, new profiles! Check around! Ask around! Childish profiles….. cartoons, saying 99% rate, over posting… constantly being aggressive….. telegram scams, or switching back and forth between telegrams and discords (wishy washy) posting very bait-like content….

title: Thesis: $SPY 690 — The K2 Zone
body:
We are approaching SPY 690, and that number matters more than people want to admit. Not because it’s just another round number but because it’s altitude. This is thin air. This is no man’s land. We are higher than we’ve ever been, with less oxygen, less volume, and more risk per step than at any point in market history.

Volume is anemic. Not because “nothing is happening,” but because everyone is distracted. End of year. Holidays. Travel. Santa rallies and cookie-cutter narratives. Desks are half staffed, conviction is low, and participation is shallow. This is not broad-based belief this is drift. The market is moving up not because of strength…but because there’s nobody left pushing back.

*That’s how you end up in no man’s land*



*Climbing K2 isn’t like climbing Everest. Everest is commercialized. Roped. Crowded. Predictable.
K2 is unforgiving.
No rescue. No margin for error. Every step costs more oxygen than the last. Every breath burns*

That’s where we are right now.

Even with MAGs down, price is still levitating. That should set off alarms. When leadership weakens but the index grinds higher anyway, that’s not health that’s mechanical support. This is not organic buying. This is structure-driven price action.

Which leads to the uncomfortable truth:

This Is a False Rally

False rallies don’t feel scary at first. They feel calm. Quiet. Almost boring….
Low VIX. Low volume….. slow grind. No urgency…..

But false rallies are dangerous because they convince participants that risk no longer exists, right before risk becomes unavoidable.

Market makers are not stupid.
They didn’t wake up last week and say “imma wing this.”
This terrain was mapped six months ago.

They are the Sherpas / Market Makers 

They know where liquidity thins
They know where positioning gets trapped
They know where retail runs out of oxygen.

And right now, they’re guiding price into a zone where one bad step matters.

The Oxygen Problem…… 

As we move into the afternoon, oxygen matters. Liquidity matters. Volume matters.
Without it, price doesn’t trend….it slips fucking hard 

At these levels, the market needs constant inflows just to stand still. If those inflows pause….. even briefly …..gravity takes over. And gravity at this altitude is brutal.

This is not a place for bravado.
This is not a place for oversized conviction.
This is a place for respect.

Conclusion

SPY 690 is not bullish by default
It is dangerous by location

We are in no man’s land.
The air is thin.
Every breath costs premium.
Every step carries risk.

Guide yourself accordingly!

title: How did DOGE miss this one? Tim Walz state,,,,
Opinion Student Loan Garnishment doesn’t remove traders: It removes demand …
body:
Nurses. Doctors. Lawyers. Teachers. You name it.

They’ve been kicking the can on student loans for years while:
buying homes
buying cars
raising kids
stacking 401
investing
living normal, solid middle-to-upper-class lives

And honestly? Why wouldn’t they gamble?

For multiple administrations now, student loan relief has been a core campaign message. Pauses, forgiveness talk, income-based plans, endless extensions. If the signal for years is “don’t worry about it, we’ll handle it”, a lot of rational people are going to say, fine I’ll allocate my money elsewhere.

Now here’s where I’ll add something most people don’t have perspective on.

For 14 years of my life, I had access to credit reports come with the territory of selling cars. I’ve seen everything  from people who couldn’t rub two rocks together to people taking 1.9% financing with 800+ scores.

And let me tell you something plainly:
There is a very real bubble of doctors, lawyers, teachers, and nurses who absolutely have the ability to pay their student loans they just haven’t been.

Not because they’re broke.
Not because they’re irresponsible.

Because the word student loan stopped existing in their mental budget. They assumed it would get handled eventually.

These people have:
investments
retirement accounts
good credit
stable jobs

They just don’t want to pay because they didn’t have to.



What? The music just stopped …..




Wage garnishment means money comes out before it hits the checking account. That doesn’t crash the market tomorrow but it does change behavior. Less discretionary spending. Less retail. More credit stress over time.

So yeah I love you Bob but saying this has zero market impact misses the second order effects. Wage garnishment doesn’t stop traders from trading. It stops people from buying Victoria’s Secret, going out to dinner, upgrading cars.

Not a problem today.
But it absolutely becomes one down the road.

That’s just reality.

body:
It’s truly no different than downloading the Robinhood app and depositing money into an account and deciding that you want to buy a stock…. Or if you want to wheel option trading, or 0 day spy calls or puts…. Etc… 

It’s a choice. It’s a choice unfortunately most people stop at “how to start a business” and look at a fee schedule that in all cost the average American less then a couple days to do, and less then a grand. But remember like we discussed in this series before this (all in my post history) even the government / state has programs to help you pay for that a start the business.  It’s just pure laziness.  

The government knows you exist.

That’s the shift.

That’s when it starts eating at you

You wake up and think:
“Okay… I’m a business owner now. I can’t pretend I’m not.”

You exist.

And once you exist, you don’t want to just exist.
You want to justify it.
You want to earn it.
You want to make it real

That’s why people who’ve done it even the ones who failed will tell you the same thing

“I’d pay triple to do it all over again”

Because it rewires you
You stop thinking like an employee
You stop asking permission
You start asking how

Here’s the part nobody tells you:

A lot of people don’t even get the idea for the business until after they start the LLC
The LLC creates the pressure
The pressure creates clarity

That’s also why second LLCs usually aren’t started out of “passion.”
They’re started out of need.

The first one teaches you what you don’t know.
The second one is built to survive

1. Momentum beats perfection every single time.
Bad logo. Bad website. Bad first idea.
Doesn’t matter. You’re moving. That’s the edge.

2. Separate the money immediately.
Business account. Even if it’s empty.
Your brain needs the line drawn.

3. Track something, not everything.
Revenue in. Money out. That’s it at first.
You don’t need spreadsheets that make you feel smart.

4. Tell fewer people.
Most people will project their fear onto your idea.
Build quietly. Announce loudly later.

5. Treat consistency like oxygen.
One small action every day beats one big burst once a month.
Miss days ……you drift. Drift ……you quit.

6. Expect the “oh shit” phase.
It comes right after the excitement wears off.
That’s not failure……. This is when you should get excited !

7. Remember: you can always shut it down!
This isn’t prison…….
Knowing you can walk away is what gives you the balls to stay

title: New Year & A New Perspective
body:
I was inspired last night by something Anderson Cooper talked about last night about the ball drop.  He said, I think some of the folks watching here right now might be watching this right now from a different place than those in the crowd. 

He stated one of the first times he watched the ball drop
Was in 1977 with his brother and dad, and that his dad  was sick and they knew he was bad, but didn’t know how bad, and five days later he went on to pass, and then his brother 10 years after that….. he remembered that night many years ago watching Dick Clark, and all the shots of the crowd we saw last evening. All the merriment and joy, and how he had never felt so alone. 

And I mention this tonight because you might be reading this, you might feel alone, even if others are around you. 

Maybe someone you love is sick, or maybe they already crossed that mysterious threshold that we virtually don’t know anything about… and you long to see them, feel them again or hear from them again…. Or maybe it’s you’re mom or dad or you’re sibling, or you’re spouse, a partner, or a child…a best friend, or maybe even an animal. Maybe it’s your job, your  health, your hope that’s gone. 

I just want you to know in the midst of all of this, which is not really real, and what you are feeling is, and you are not the only one…. You might feel alone tonight going into the new year, but you are not alone. So wherever you are in the world, or in your grief, you are not alone…. You are here with us, and I am grateful we are together. 

Stay Beautiful, 
- Freeballer 2026

title: The Middle Candle
body:
If you don’t know about the middle candle you are leaving money on the table….




Most traders wait for the close
That’s why they’re late

SPY and QQQ don’t decide at the close  they decide in the middle

The midpoint of a 5-min or 15-min candle is where the fight actually happens
Above it -  buyers are accepting price.
Below it  - sellers are leaning on it

You wanna know if a move is real?
Don’t look at the wick
Don’t stare at indicator
Watch what price does when it comes back to the middle.

Strong move - pulls back  - holds the midpoint  
continues
Fake move  - pulls back  - loses the midpoint  -rotation, chop, premium bleed.

That’s not magical 
That’s algos measuring fair value in real time

Institutions don’t buy the close
They scale around averages
Read this again  

They scale around averages. 

Remember they scale around average’s   
The midpoint is the fastest way to see who’s in control before Twitter knows

If SPY keeps rejecting the middle, stop forcing direction.
If it accepts above it, stop overthinking

Freeballer rules 
If price can’t hold the middle, it doesn’t deserve your money

Most blown accounts aren’t from bad entries 
they’re from trading inside the candle with no read on control.

Watch the middle.
Everything else is noise

venezuela update:
The real reason the US is invading Venezuela goes back to a deal Henry Kissinger made with Saudi Arabia in 1974.
why this is actually about the SURVIVAL of the US dollar itself.

Not drugs. Not terrorism. Not "democracy."

This is about the petrodollar system that has kept America the dominant economic power for 50 years.

And Venezuela just threatened to end it.

Here's what really just happened:

Venezuela has 303 billion barrels of proven oil reserves.

The largest on Earth.

More than Saudi Arabia.

20% of the entire world's oil.

But here's the part that matters:

Venezuela was actively selling that oil in Chinese yuan. Not dollars.

In 2018, Venezuela announced it would "free itself from the dollar."

They started accepting yuan, euros, rubles, anything BUT dollars for oil.

They were petitioning to join BRICS.

They were building direct payment channels with China that bypass SWIFT entirely.

And they were sitting on enough oil to fund de-dollarization for decades.

Why does this matter?

Because the entire American financial system is built on one thing:

The petrodollar.

In 1974, Henry Kissinger made a deal with Saudi Arabia:

All oil sold globally must be priced in US dollars.

In exchange, America provides military protection.

This single agreement created artificial demand for dollars worldwide.

Every country on Earth needs dollars to buy oil.

This lets America print unlimited money while other countries work for it.

It funds the military. The welfare state. The deficit spending.

The petrodollar is more important to US hegemony than aircraft carriers.

And there's a pattern of what happens to leaders who challenge it:

2000: Saddam Hussein announces Iraq will sell oil in euros instead of dollars.

2003: Invaded. Regime change. Iraq's oil immediately switched back to dollars. Saddam lynched.

The WMDs were never found because they never existed.

2009: Gaddafi proposes a gold-backed African currency called the "gold dinar" for oil trade.

Email quote: "This gold was intended to establish a pan-African currency based on the Libyan golden Dinar."

2011: NATO bombs Libya. Gaddafi sodomized and murdered. Libya now has open slave markets.

"We came, we saw, he died!" Clinton laughed on camera.

With FIVE TIMES more oil than Saddam and Gaddafi combined.

Actively selling in yuan.

Building payment systems outside dollar control.

Petitioning to join BRICS.

Partnered with China, Russia, and Iran.

The three countries leading global de-dollarization.

This isn't coincidence.

Challenge the petrodollar. Get regime changed.

Every. Single. Time.

"American sweat, ingenuity and toil created the oil industry in Venezuela. Its tyrannical expropriation was the largest recorded theft of American wealth and property."

He's not hiding it.

They're claiming Venezuelan oil BELONGS to America because US companies developed it 100 years ago.

By this logic, every nationalized resource in history was "theft."

But here's the DEEPER problem:

The petrodollar is already dying.

Russia sells oil in rubles and yuan since Ukraine.

Saudi Arabia is openly discussing yuan settlements.

Iran has been trading in non-dollar currencies for years.

China built CIPS, their own alternative to SWIFT with 4,800 banks in 185 countries.

Venezuela joining BRICS with 303 billion barrels of oil would accelerate this exponentially.

January 3rd, 1990. Panama invaded. Noriega captured.

When the world realizes the petrodollar is maintained by violence?

title: Documenting $ORBS DD Part I with @squeezekid
body:
I want to just say I applaud this level of commitment to using vocabulary like “unlikely” and speaking on behalf of personal loss.  And showing transparency. 

That’s what is required now, this isn’t 2025 anymore. This isn’t the “neverpullover” and “squeezekid” show…. It’s the adults with money and degrees and access to education as well as reporting financial crimes. 

The original post’s hypothetical full $125 million buyback at $2, reducing shares to 135 million is optimistic at best. The program was approved December 29, 2025, but execution isn’t guaranteed. Current cash is only $23.73 million (MRQ), with stables adding to ~$69 million. To hit $125 million, they’d likely dip into crypto holdings, risking the very asset value bulls tout.
Even if executed:
•  Volatility Amplification: Yes, a lower float (float currently 100.52 million) increases swings. But in a down market, that means sharper drops. Short interest is 11.81 million (6.17% of float) notable but not gamma-squeeze territory like GameStop. Covering could provide a pop, but without fundamental catalysts, it’s fleeting.
•  Premium Pricing: Post-buyback, at 135 million shares, $20 implies a $2.7 billion market cap. That’s 10x current NAV, assuming no WLD growth. Profoundly unrealistic unless WLD hits moonshot levels (e.g., $10+), which ignores its controversies.
•  Timing and Reality: The post admits a “steady rally” could take a month. But with the announcement fresh, any initial hype has faded price is flat around $1.97. Steady rallies require inflows; here, it’s retail speculation.


1.97 at best. 



Don’t want to let anything get deleted….

This is what we’re really trying to build here on AfterHours.

As you navigate through AfterHours and you are new, take a look around at who’s who and what’s what … say to yourself why someone who might have fake followers or manufactured tips… read through, who are they mutual  friends with… why do you see profiles with followers who are not active … why do you see loops of information that’s vague…. Those are not the folks looking out in the best interest of you. 



$ONDS is just an example…..The bigger lesson is this: real movement in the market requires volume, open interest, and delta working together. You need real participation, real conviction, real catalysts. But even that isn’t enough by itself. It also has to be a company with morals, ethics, values, and somewhere to go. Something worth standing behind.

When those things connect… when the data lines up and the story lines up… and you start to see people rally around a message those people stop feeling like followers.

They feel like guardians.

And that’s the beautiful thing about AfterHours. There are people here who believe in guardians. People who value protection over hype. People who want to defend portfolios, not exploit them.

Look at nature. Certain dog breeds were bred to guard. Not to attack, not to show off but to protect.
Drones are guardians. Watchtowers are guardians. The best leaders are guardians.

And there are guardians on this app too
People who want to help others grow.
People who don’t want you to be exit liquidity.
People who don’t scream “BUY NOW” just so they can dump on you eleven dollars higher.

That’s the difference. That’s the line in the sand.

What we’re building here is education over hype. Structure over chaos. Volume, open interest, delta backed by integrity. Backed by community. Backed by people who actually give a damn if you succeed.

Find your guardians.
Be a guardian for others.
That’s the mission

title: Markets After a Holiday Monday: What to Expect
body:
Holiday weeks aren’t normal trading weeks. Liquidity dries out …… volume gets weird af, and a lot of the “smarter money” isn’t fully back until midweek…. 

That’s why Tuesday–Wednesday often set the real tones

Here’s what typically happens….

Low volume /fake moves
Price can rip or dump on air………Breakouts fail more often! Stops get hunted 

Algos  run wild
With fewer real orders, algorithms can push price around tho 

Chop increases

 Retail overreacts …… chase moves that wouldn’t exist in a normal week.


The real moves often comes midweek
Thursday and Friday are usually where conviction shows up

How to prepare 

Be picker on entry’s.  
Thea will kick and move.
