title: My thesis on why $BTC is stroking out….
body:
There’s a lot of ETFs that are proxies of Bitcoin…. So the initial view on that was that we had all these different vehicles out there to bring in more liquidity the bitcoin market more driving and it keeps the price up ….. 

Now all these ETFs are negative outflows…more money obviously is going out of the ETF then coming in… 

ALL The ETFs are getting slammed right now…. So this ETF idea being another catalyst isn’t cracking out so well. 

It’s gone upside down. 

You also have this cascading liquidity effect right now as well…. A snowball if you will. 

Most of the bitcoin market is levered. What does that mean? People borrow money to go and buy it…. You’ve had all these people who believed in this so much they borrowed against 401Ks! And are still having money pulled from paychecks for MSTR and ETH-A 

So guess what happens when the LTV is to high? (Loan to value) you cannot hold it anymore. 

You can only have so much debt against it.  So we’re seeing margin calls up the wazoo right? 

Because it’s to leveraged now… based on the firm or platform decided … so those forced sales are causing this chain reaction. 

So what happens to the price and the assholes that Schilled it? They shut the fuck up, and have to work and have a paycheck garnished from the 401k. 

And then this triggers more action to drop the price even more.

title: The Part of the Economy No One Wants to talk about….
body:
I have kind of a boring job for the most part, and if it gets exciting and you see the rolling suitcase and Bookbag coming out and I am flying around we are in trouble  

Lately commercial insurance fraud cases are on the rise in more epic ways then you can understand and how it’s attached to the data I am going to start to share with you.

Landlords and tenants come up with more creative solutions and ways to pay bills when things are headed for a rough time. Cold weather is a perfect crime to hide and “wash” away the sins that can transpire between an old toilet in a basement next to a server room and electric panels. Millions of dollars in fraud claims  



What’s this data… 

If 1 in 14 of these massive commercial property loans is late or in trouble, that’s not normal trouble ……it’s a credit system warning

Office buildings aren’t just empty their owners can’t afford the bills anymore

Bank of America thinks that the stock market’s “easy” leadership era is buckling, and it’s not because the economy is suddenly falling apart.

In a Friday note reported by Business Insider, Michael Hartnett’s team argued that the early-2020s era, when Big Tech (and the Magnificent 7) could do no wrong, is over, and that it’s time to watch the market segments that actually look like the economy.


A big part of that is that the AI boom is effectively dragging hyperscalers into a significantly heavier spending cycle.

For some context, the four leading tech giants in Google-parent Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, and Meta have collectively guided to nearly $635–$665 billion of 2026 capex linked to AI data centers/chips.

With such colossal capex numbers, there are also considerations around valuation and stock buybacks, which have fueled tech stocks for years.

On top of that, Hartnett links the next phase of stock market leadership to politics. With President Donald Trump pushing hard on affordability, BofA makes the case that the pressure then falls on the biggest targets, which shifts where investors want to hide.

	•	Understand complex contexts — not just keywords or surface-level inputs, but meaning, intent, and nuance across text, speech, and visual data.
	•	Synthesize knowledge across domains, blending medicine, law, engineering, arts, and science under one reasoning framework.
	•	Perform tasks we currently think require “real intelligence” — like strategic planning, nuanced negotiation, creative design, and scientific hypothesis formation.

This is driven by improved model architectures, larger datasets, and smarter self-learning techniques.

⸻

🧠 2. AI Will Think More Like Humans (But Not Exactly Like Humans)

By 2030, we expect AI that:
	•	Retains memory over long conversations and interactions
	•	Understands multi-step reasoning and cross-domain logic
	•	Shows emergent problem-solving behavior (not just pattern matching)
These improvements will make AI more useful, trustworthy, and context-aware.

But it’s important to note: AI won’t have human consciousness, emotions, or true self-awareness — at least not in the psychological sense people often imagine.

⸻

🏠 3. AI in Everyday Life

Nearly every home, phone, and device will likely have a personal AI assistant that can:
	•	Plan your schedule intelligently
	•	Automate tasks like booking flights or managing finances
	•	Personalize learning and entertainment
	•	Monitor health and well-being in real time

Think of AI assistants that are proactive, not reactive — suggesting actions before you even ask.

⸻

🏢 4. AI in the Workplace

Across industries, AI will:
	•	Automate repetitive and analytical work (data entry, coding assistance, legal document review, diagnostics)
	•	Augment human creativity (design tools, marketing content, engineering optimization)
	•	Act as “co-pilots” rather than replacements — boosting productivity and quality.

Some routine jobs may disappear, but many new ones will be created, especially in AI oversight, ethics, safety engineering, and prompt design.

⸻

🧬 5. AI in Medicine and Science

By 2030, AI could:
	•	Accelerate drug discovery
	•	Predict health outcomes from genetics and behavior
	•	Personalize treatment plans
	•	Interpret medical scans with superhuman accuracy

AI might help democratize high-quality healthcare globally.

⸻

📱 6. AI-Generated Content Everywhere

Expect:
	•	Movies, music, books, and games co-created with AI
	•	Realistic virtual humans and interactive characters
	•	Hyperpersonalized media recommendations

The creative process will become more collaborative between humans and machines.

⸻

🔐 7. AI Safety and Governance

As AI becomes more powerful, we’ll likely see:
	•	Global AI safety standards
	•	Certification regimes for high-risk AI systems
	•	Stronger regulation to prevent misuse
	•	New legal frameworks for AI liability and responsibility

This won’t be universal by 2030, but momentum is building.

⸻

🌍 8. Societal and Ethical Shifts

By 2030:
	•	AI ethics will be mainstream
	•	People will demand accountability, transparency, and fairness
	•	New norms around data privacy and digital rights will emerge

Public debates about AI’s role in elections, employment, privacy, and human agency will shape policy worldwide.

⸻

📉 What AI Won’t Fully Achieve by 2030

Despite rapid progress, AI likely will not have:
	•	Human-like consciousness
	•	Genuine emotions or subjective experience
	•	Perfect understanding of abstract human values without explicit guidance
	•	Autonomous moral judgment

It will be powerful — but still a tool shaped and directed by humans.

Imagine everyone suddenly has less money for snacks and toys.

What do people do?

They start looking for the biggest box for the cheapest price.

That’s basically why Costco does so well when the economy gets rough

If money gets tight, people stop shopping at expensive stores.
Instead they go somewhere they can buy A LOT of stuff for less money
Costco sells giant packs of food/paper towels, and essentials for cheaper per item

So when people are trying to stretch their money 
Costco suddenly becomes the smartest place to shop

Costco makes people buy a membership first

Once someone pays for that membership, there mind says  I must get my money back 

“I better shop here a lot so I get my money’s worth”

title: Why we are powerful….
body:
A Note on the $100 Bill:
According to Federal Reserve data, more than 60% of all $100 bills actually circulate outside of the United States. In many developing nations, "Benjamins" are the gold standard for private savings because they hold their value better than local banknotes during inflation.

1. Argentina
Argentina is widely considered the #1 holder of U.S. $100 bills per capita outside the United States. Due to decades of high inflation and distrust in the local peso, Argentines hold an estimated $200 billion in physical U.S. cash—mostly in $100 bills—stored in "under-the-mattress" savings (known locally as colchón).
2. Russia
Historically, Russia has been one of the largest importers of physical $100 bills. Even with modern sanctions, the dollar remains the primary "hard currency" for private savings and high-value black market transactions across the region.
3. Ecuador
As a fully "dollarized" economy, Ecuador uses the USD for everything. While smaller bills circulate for daily coffee and groceries, the $100 bill is the standard for real estate, car sales, and bank-level savings.
4. Cambodia
Cambodia is unofficially dollarized. ATMs often dispense U.S. dollars by default, and most businesses price items in USD. The $100 bill is the preferred note for paying rent, salaries, and large business invoices.
5. Panama
Panama has a century-long history with the dollar. Because it is a global banking and shipping hub, massive amounts of $100 bills move through its economy daily.
6. Zimbabwe
After experiencing some of the worst hyperinflation in history, Zimbabweans almost entirely abandoned their local currency in favor of the USD. Large denominations like the $100 bill are prized because they are easier to store than mountains of local notes.
7. Lebanon
Following the recent collapse of the Lebanese Pound, the economy has become "cash-based" and heavily reliant on the $100 bill. It is now common to see grocery stores and restaurants listing prices in dollars.
8. Vietnam
While the Vietnamese Dong is the official currency, $100 bills are a standard "store of wealth." Many families keep gold or $100 bills as a hedge against the fluctuating value of the Dong.

I’ve documented over 700 telegram scammers with the support of this community over the last year! They change names and telegrams like it’s a job. Because the job they have is to scam you! You are the profit. 

⚠️ READ ⚠️ 
If it’s a telegram ! Stay away! Stay away from telegram scammers! 

As tax returns come in, be on the look out! India is taking charge and bringing these networks down. They are all part of an Indian and Chinese network dedicated to scamming. 




The list of the ones just today. (Active on Sundays) 
These guys want 100-150+ dollars a month just to take your money. 

🧠 How Telegram Trading Scammers Actually Work

1. 🎯 Step 1: Attraction (Hook You In)

They find you through:
	•	TikTok / Instagram comments
	•	Cold DMs (“I made $5k today, want signals?”)
	•	Ads or fake testimonials
	•	“Free signal groups”

They promise:
	•	“Guaranteed returns”
	•	“90% win rate”
	•	“AI bot never loses”  ￼

👉 That’s your first red flag — no real trader talks like that.

⸻

2. 🧲 Step 2: Build Credibility (Fake Authority)

Inside the Telegram group, they:
	•	Post ONLY winning trades
	•	Delete losing trades
	•	Show fake P&L screenshots
	•	Use titles like:
	•	“Professor”
	•	“Senior analyst”
	•	“Fund manager”

Reddit users describe it perfectly:

“They deliberately showcase only winning trades”  ￼

👉 It creates the illusion: “Everyone is making money but me”

⸻

3. 💰 Step 3: Small Wins to Hook You

This is where it gets dangerous.

They’ll:
	•	Let you make a small profit
	•	Or fake a dashboard showing profits
	•	Sometimes even allow a small withdrawal

Real example:
	•	Victim was allowed to withdraw small amounts before being drained later  ￼

👉 This is psychological — it builds trust.

⸻

4. 🪤 Step 4: The Big Ask (Where People Get Trapped)

Now they push you into one of these:

A. “Let us trade for you”
	•	“We’ll manage your account”
	•	“Send funds, we’ll grow it”

B. Fake trading platform
	•	You deposit money into THEIR site
	•	It shows fake profits

C. VIP upgrade
	•	“Pay $500–$5,000 for premium signals”

👉 Reality:
	•	The money is gone immediately
	•	The “trading” is fake

⸻

5. 🧾 Step 5: The Fee Trap (Milk You Dry)

Once you try to withdraw:
They hit you with:
	•	“Tax fee”
	•	“Liquidity fee”
	•	“Withdrawal fee”
	•	“AML verification”

Real case:
	•	Victim asked to pay tax and service charges to withdraw profits  ￼

👉 You never get your money — just more fees.

⸻

6. 🚫 Step 6: Exit / Ghosting

Eventually:
	•	They stop responding
	•	Website disappears
	•	Telegram account deleted

OR…

They hit you with:
👉 “Deposit more to recover losses”

⸻

⚠️ The “We Manage Your Money” Angle (Big One You Asked About)

This is one of the most common hooks:

They say:
	•	“You don’t need experience”
	•	“We trade for you”
	•	“Hands-free income”

What’s really happening:
	•	It’s either:
	•	A Ponzi setup
	•	Or straight theft

Scam pattern:
	1.	You send money
	2.	They show fake growth
	3.	Ask for more
	4.	Disappear


🚨 Biggest Red Flags (Memorize These)

If you see ANY of these — it’s a scam:
	•	“Guaranteed profits”
	•	“We trade for you”
	•	“Pay to withdraw”
	•	“VIP signals”
	•	“AI bot never loses”
	•	Random DM about trading




Beware ‼️

title: Poll: Was this week better than imagined?
Bulls checking in on the bears ….
Check out this retard …. @Legitimate_Risk
body:
Man, been waiting a month to make this post. So here it goes, this fella and I have always treated each other in a gentlemanly manor, and what started off as a discord just to house and entertain a small extension of less then 10 people turned into something more then I guess could have truly ever imagined. 

This app is kinda really special to me, but more so like the friendships and bonds I share with some really special people. I’d tag everyone who had a hand in Pathfinders. But I thank them over and over again privately, and it’s one of those, “you’ve helped create things for us too” type of deals. 

And then there’s this guy….. I love inspiring people with you, I love how you somehow tame me down a little bit, I adore screaming at people to stay outta shit they don’t belong in, I love growing something with you, and taking a really awesome group of people into places that are special. 

I love everyone’s little hand in the discord, anyone who wanted to build something, have a hand in something, was given full administrative access to anything they wanted, at one point this platform had 6 people who were founders and could delete this discord off the face of the earth for all
They cared or wanted.

When I started this discord I asked someone who I think the moon and back of if it was OK…. I was careful of peoples feelings I care about along the way too, because freeballer is a large extension of what this community is. 

I am to the point, and the community we’ve built around is to the point too, we’re here to accomplish one thing. Make
Money, and support other discords, and support other people.  I know at times I’m a douche bag, and at times you might feel as if am “piggy-backing” off you’re shit. 

The truth is, and this even goes for my haters, or people who do not see eye to eye with me. 

1) I’ve always liked you’re shit 
2) I’ve always supported a majority of everyone’s shit on here 
3) I continue and have always as much as possible attended your trivia shit, the launches of your YouTubes, and even you’re first day doing a live. @gr8ripple and Iwere the only two dudes one day listening to @mphinance be technically challenged showing us what he built for 45 minutes and explain shit that was so technical I didn’t understand it, but clapped along. 

4) last night, I watched a young man who makes an amazing product sit down with a mom, and someone I know better then my own at times who I’ve spent 8 months trading with on average four days a week challenge another man to make
His product better, and by the end of the presentation she was amazed and called me an hour later, because she sat there and played with it. 

5) watched a kid this week tell me how sad he was to go To his retail job he hates because he was so happy to 3k this week. And road out the shit plays with us for 5 weeks too… and we begged him to sit on his hands and not trade. He listened. 

6) Sunday someone who probably still hates me, took two questions from me as I listened to a live, and said “that’s a good question… twice” …. Ya know… that fucking meant something really big to me, because it made me smile. 

7) watched a member this week have his kid, and share how thrilled he was to share in a moment with us. 





So…. Cheers to many more memories, to the 15 folks who help and babysit our discord because you want to ginnie pig  us, and install free shit that makes people better and more aware traders, I cannot ever repay you enough, starting this discord was like buying an old house that was down to a frame, and the people who just came out of the woodwork.

Have a wonderful weekend, 

Let’s leave people better off then found sometimes. 

- White Freeballer

June 4th PDT restrictions lift for accounts below 25,000 ….. oh boy….. nice knowing some of you folks…..
body:
Some don’t folks are going to absolutely use margin and blow up an account, I can easily see some college kid spending all summer FOMING crayon drawings and buying shit from some guru who makes one call…. 

This isn’t going to end well for many. 

What does all this mean :

 

The old PDT rule kept millions of smaller accounts from actively scalping or day trading. Once that barrier disappears, a lot of people with $1k–$10k accounts suddenly gain the ability to trade intraday freely on margin.  

Here’s what traders are expecting almost immediately:

More volatility intraday

You’ll likely see:

* Harder morning pumps
* Faster reversals
* More fake breakouts
* Bigger lunchtime flushes
* Increased gamma squeezes from retail options flow

Retail traders tend to pile into the same tickers at once, especially from social platforms like TikTok, X/Twitter, Discord, Reddit, and apps like AfterHour.

Brokers and trading apps benefit first

Companies tied to retail activity could see increased revenue from:

* Payment for order flow
* Options volume
* Margin interest
* Increased account openings

That’s why stocks tied to retail trading jumped when the rule change was announced.  

Likely beneficiaries include:

* Robinhood￼
* Webull￼
* TradeStation￼
* Interactive Brokers￼

Small accounts may gravitate toward higher-risk trades

A major concern regulators and analysts brought up is that many traders with smaller balances may chase:

* 0DTE SPY/SPX options
* Weekly lotto contracts
* Leveraged ETFs
* Fast momentum names

That can create sharper retail-driven moves and potentially increase “YOLO” behavior.  

Liquidity could improve in some names

More active traders means:

* More bids/asks
* More participation
* Faster fills in heavily traded stocks

That can actually help short-term traders in liquid names like:

* SPY
* QQQ
* TSLA
* NVDA

The market itself probably won’t fundamentally change overnight

Institutions still dominate overall market volume. But what probably changes quickly is the texture of the market:

* More retail participation
* Faster momentum moves
* More options-driven volatility
* Stronger social-media-driven pumps

The biggest immediate impact may honestly be on options flow and intraday momentum trading, not long-term investing.

Small and Mid Cap Stocks after June 4th PDT Rule Changes Things…
body:
Let’s get our heads out of our asses. 
This is huge for the market. 


$ONDS *cough*
$HIMS 

Small caps and mid caps are where retail traders dominate momentum trading. Lowering the barrier from $25k to $2k means:

* More retail participation
* More intraday scalping
* More momentum chasing
* More volume in lower-float names
* More options speculation spilling into equities

That tends to disproportionately hit:

* biotech runners
* AI/speculative tech
* low-float momentum stocks
* meme stocks
* SPAC-style speculative names

The mega caps like Apple or Microsoft already have institutional liquidity. Small caps move harder when retail money floods in.

Reuters and WSJ both noted the rule change could “turbocharge retail trading” and increase YOLO-style activity. 



What likely happens immediately

If this rolls out fully across brokers:

1. Higher volume in small caps

Stocks that previously traded:

* 5M shares/day
    may suddenly trade:
* 20–50M shares/day

because thousands of smaller accounts can finally day trade aggressively.



2. More violent squeezes

Low-float names become easier to squeeze when:

* more traders can rapidly re-enter positions
* traders are not “locked out” after 3 day trades
* traders can compound gains intraday

That creates:

* faster gamma squeezes
* stronger premarket moves
* larger after-hours volatility



3. More pump-and-dump behavior

This is the negative side.

Small caps are already easier to manipulate. Removing PDT restrictions increases:

* Discord pump groups
* TikTok/Twitter momentum swarms
* fake “breakout” moves
* afternoon rug pulls

Especially in:

* OTCs
* microcaps
* low-float NASDAQ names

Regulators are openly concerned about this.  



Why market makers may love this

Firms tied to retail order flow benefit from:

* more trades
* more options volume
* more spread capture
* more payment for order flow revenue

That’s partly why brokerages like Robinhood￼ and Webull￼ reacted positively to the changes.  


The medium-term reality

This probably creates:

* more liquidity
* more retail engagement
* more speculation
* higher volatility

But eventually:

* many undercapitalized traders likely blow up accounts quickly
* intraday margin calls increase
* brokers tighten risk controls on volatile names

So the long-term effect may be:

* short-term speculative boom
* followed by higher broker restrictions on certain tickers

title: If you believe it, show it.
body:
Anyone can post a thesis, draw lines on a chart, or explain why they believe something should happen. What separates real market participants from spectators is the willingness to show positioning, executions, risk, and accountability. That is where trust is built.

Transparency matters because not everyone is trading the same size, the same contracts, or the same risk profile. A trader with a large account can survive volatility very differently than someone trading a handful of contracts. If people follow an idea without understanding the actual execution, the strike selection, the timing, or the risk exposure involved, they can end up taking far more damage than intended.

That is why showing positions and executions is important. It gives context. It allows people to understand whether someone is truly participating in the trade or simply narrating from the sidelines. It also helps protect the people listening. Someone buying deeper in the money, sizing incorrectly, or entering late because they believed in your conviction can suffer *real losses* if the full picture is not communicated honestly.

Reputation in this business is built over time and destroyed quickly. *Protecting it matters* Growing it matters even more. Accountability, transparency, and skin in the game are what separate credibility from performance art.

I know some people have strong personal opinions about me, and that is fine. But one thing nobody can say is that I speak without participation. I believe in having skin in the game. I believe if you are going to talk conviction, you should be willing to stand behind it publicly.

Because at the end of the day, 
No Ticky, No Laundry 

Receipts.

title: Look at you fuckers…..
How I live my life….
body:
Just about every time I see someone I stop. I kind of got out of the habit in the last couple of years, moved to a big city and all that, my girlfriend wasn't too stoked on the practice. Then some shit happened to me that changed me and I am back to offering rides habitually. If you would indulge me, it is long story and has almost nothing to do with hitch hiking other than happening on a road.

This past year I have had 3 instances of car trouble. A blow out on a freeway, a bunch of blown fuses and an out of gas situation. All of them were while driving other people's cars which, for some reason, makes it worse on an emotional level. It makes it worse on a practical level as well, what with the fact that I carry things like a jack and extra fuses in my car, and know enough not to park, facing downhill, on a steep incline with less than a gallon of fuel.

Anyway, each of these times this shit happened I was DISGUSTED with how people would not bother to help me. I spent hours on the side of the freeway waiting, watching roadside assistance vehicles blow past me, for AAA to show. The 4 gas stations I asked for a gas can at told me that they couldn't loan them out "for my safety" but I could buy a really shitty 1-gallon one with no cap for $15. It was enough, each time, to make you say shit like "this country is going to hell in a handbasket."

But you know who came to my rescue all three times? Immigrants. Mexican immigrants. None of them spoke a lick of the language. But one of those dudes had a profound affect on me.

He was the guy that stopped to help me with a blow out with his whole family of 6 in tow. I was on the side of the road for close to 4 hours. Big jeep, blown rear tire, had a spare but no jack. I had signs in the windows of the car, big signs that said NEED A JACK and offered money. No dice. Right as I am about to give up and just hitch out there a van pulls over and dude bounds out. He sizes the situation up and calls for his youngest daughter who speaks english. He conveys through her that he has a jack but it is too small for the Jeep so we will need to brace it. He produces a saw from the van and cuts a log out of a downed tree on the side of the road. We rolled it over, put his jack on top, and bam, in business. I start taking the wheel off and, if you can believe it, I broke his tire iron. It was one of those collapsible ones and I wasn't careful and I snapped the head I needed clean off. Fuck.

No worries, he runs to the van, gives it to his wife and she is gone in a flash, down the road to buy a tire iron. She is back in 15 minutes, we finish the job with a little sweat and cussing (stupid log was starting to give), and I am a very happy man. We are both filthy and sweaty. The wife produces a large water jug for us to wash our hands in. I tried to put a 20 in the man's hand but he wouldn't take it so I instead gave it to his wife as quietly as I could. I thanked them up one side and down the other. I asked the little girl where they lived, thinking maybe I could send them a gift for being so awesome. She says they live in Mexico. They are here so mommy and daddy can pick peaches for the next few weeks. After that they are going to pick cherries then go back home. She asks if I have had lunch and when I told her no she gave me a tamale from their cooler, the best fucking tamale I have ever had.

So, to clarify, a family that is undoubtedly poorer than you, me, and just about everyone else on that stretch of road, working on a seasonal basis where time is money, took an hour or two out of their day to help some strange dude on the side of the road when people in tow trucks were just passing me by. Wow...

But we aren't done yet. I thank them again and walk back to my car and open the foil on the tamale cause I am starving at this point and what do I find inside? My fucking $20 bill! I whirl around and run up to the van and the guy rolls his window down. He sees the $20 in my hand and just shaking his head no like he won't take it. All I can think to say is "Por Favor, Por Favor, Por Favor" with my hands out. Dude just smiles, shakes his head and, with what looked like great concentration, tried his hardest to speak to me in English:

"Today you.... tomorrow me."

Rolled up his window, drove away, his daughter waving to me in the rear view. I sat in my car eating the best fucking tamale of all time and I just cried. Like a little girl. It has been a rough year and nothing has broke my way. This was so out of left field I just couldn't deal.

In the 5 months since I have changed a couple of tires, given a few rides to gas stations and, once, went 50 miles out of my way to get a girl to an airport. I won't accept money. Every time I tell them the same thing when we are through:

"Today you.... tomorrow me."

title: 🔔 Getting Sued from someone on AH Part: 1 🔔
body:
It’s always interesting when someone threatens to “get you arrested for defamation of character’ 

Defamation is generally a civil matter, not a criminal one. You don’t call the police because someone hurt your feelings online. You file a civil lawsuit, prove the statements were false, prove damages occurred, and then convince a court. That’s how it works! As someone from a ginormous passion and respect for the law, as well as being socially and professionally involved in court proceedings on a bi-weekly basis for very large scale and complicated investigations involving millions of dollars in fraud cases.  

The irony is that someone claiming to be a serious researcher should probably research the legal terms they’re using before posting them publicly! But also provide receipt’s!  

That said, I do want to compliment you on one thing: your confidence is incredible. The ability to threaten legal action, misuse the legal terminology, misspell half the post, and still hit “publish” without hesitation is a level of self belief most entrepreneurs can only dream of!

I genuinely respect anyone who contributes research to a community. But if you’re going to lecture others about credibility, facts, and accountability, those standards should probably start with your own posts.

The community deserves information, discussion, and evidence not emotional outbursts and legal threats based on a misunderstanding of the law

With that being said sir, I can forward my personal information to @SeymourButts I am located in the state of PA and can forward my attorney’s information to Mr @SeymourButts and I URGE you to contact him! And let’s get the ball rolling sir! 

I’ll email that now! And it’s help@afterhour.com 
I’m gonna go ahead and follow up on this in 48 hours and see if you collected your information! 

Defamation is not established because someone says something you dislike. Generally, a plaintiff must show a false statement of fact, publication to a third party… fault, and damages. If someone believes those elements exist, courts exist for a reason!

Threatening legal action repeatedly without ever taking legal action does not prove defamation occurred. It usually proves only that *YOU* made a threat.

You seem incredibly confident in your legal position. I look forward to seeing that confidence transition from an AfterHour post into an actual court proceedings

title: Senate limits Trump’s power with Iran War
body:
The Senate adopted a resolution on Tuesday directing the president to remove military forces from the conflict with Iran, a significant rebuke to Donald Trump and a strong message that the war lacks support in Congress.

Democrats have repeatedly forced votes to limit Trump’s war powers in both the House and the Senate — a campaign that has gradually picked up more GOP support in recent weeks, drawing the president’s ire.

GOP Sens. Rand Paul, Susan Collins, Lisa Murkowski and Bill Cassidy joined Democrats in voting for the resolution, while Democratic Sen. John Fetterman voted against it. The final tally was 50-48. The absences of GOP Sens. Mitch McConnell and Dave McCormick, who have previously voted against advancing war powers resolutions, contributed to the measure’s adoption.

The measure passed the House earlier this month. But because it is what’s known as a concurrent resolution, it does not require the president’s signature and, by definition, does not carry the force of law.

A White House official dismissed the Senate vote, saying the resolution “has no significance” and blaming the measure’s adoption on “Republican absences.”

“Concurrent resolutions do not go to the president and have no force of law,” the official said.

The official said the resolution directs the president to remove US armed forces from hostilities against Iran, “yet there are no hostilities from which to remove U.S. forces, as hostilities terminated with the ceasefire on April 7th.”

A House Democratic aide who has been involved in the effort to pass the war powers resolution told CNN earlier this month, however, that they believe the measure would be binding and it would be a legal matter to work out.

This is the 10th time the Senate has voted on an Iran war powers measure since the beginning of the year. An earlier Senate-led resolution advanced last month, but has not had a follow-up vote yet as Democrats work to ensure they have the support needed to pass it.

The House passed the concurrent resolution 215-208, with four House Republicans voting with Democrats and immediately facing the president’s anger. Trump called the four members “GRANDSTANDERS” and their action “unpatriotic” in a post on Truth Social after the vote.

Some Democratic senators, including Tim Kaine, have argued that passage of a war powers resolution is necessary, even after the US reached an agreement with Iran and amid ongoing negotiations with Tehran.

“I think it’s a good time to have the vote to say, ‘Hey, if we’re really in a period of maybe some stability here, let’s not just allow it to start up again without Congress being involved in that decision,” he told reporters last week.

Source: CNN

title: Freeballer Back Story: Why I am the way I am…. (Long)
body:
Someone close asked me to share, and I was inspired.  
So here ya go, and I apologize if this is long. 

My sister is younger then I, and my job as older brother was to always protect my sister from harm. Growing up I knew things would be difficult in the early and mid 90s with my sister who was born into this earth with 3 fingers on her hand. Many surgeries at a Jewish Hospital for hands in Lewisville Kentucky over the course if the small life remained a constant throughout school, along with the torment caused by kids being kids. 

Day in and day out, I sat with my sister on the school bus growing up, and listened to children chirp and say all sorts of fucked up things (my sister is a unbelievably beautiful girl)  my sisters last hand surgery to allow her to grip things when she was 9 placed me in between my sophomore year when I got my drivers license. 

I was no longer riding the school bus with my sister, I had found out through my best friends brother that a kid who has given her a hard time in the past (a 7th grader) reduced my sister in the mornings ride to tears after learning of this in my second period class, I steamed through third, and boiled onto my study hall, i utilized the hall pass for a long-walk to the other side of the school where a 7th grader who chirped at everyone was standing in the hall getting ready for his lunch. 

He didn’t go to lunch that day, he didn’t eat right for the next 4 months…. I took the time to ask him multiple times if he thought he was funny…. And he kept smirking at me, the testosterone that fueled in my body as a sophomore lead to me rearranging his face to a degree he wasn’t able to speak anymore, and was knocked out cold. I plopped myself in the office of my former grade school principals office and waited for the high school principal to show up, I heard the EMS sirens coming, and I also was faced with a local police officer, followed by what would be a state police officer taking pictures of my hands, and listening to a very calm teenager unfold the events that transpired and the choices I made. 

Prior to this, I was carrying in above average high GPA, perfect attendance for many years, and lots of pieces of paper for participating in community events, and giving my time to others as a young adult. I was active in the community. 

The young man needed a few jaw surgeries, and some stitches, and had a nice-sized knot on his head from the fall. I was later suspended from school, and almost expelled. 

Many people in the community over the following days chirped, my parents were faced with some bills I created for them, later in the afternoon the sheriffs department transported Freeballer to a juvenile detention facility where talks of “trying me as an adult” were chirped about.

I remained calm. I was released to my parents the next afternoon, and a court date was set for my face arrangements, a community of over 2,000 people wrote and stood behind me and my parents for those actions. 

I later went on to serve a in school suspension for 60 days and had to broom sweep the gym floor in the morning, and after school. My principal and I got really close, and alot of the teachers took the time to speak with me in the morning and I spent time in counseling for “anger issues” that never once were displayed.  

The parents didn’t want to press charges, they profusely apologize for the child, and the kid went on to apologize too within days of getting his wires removed. 

No one ever went on to fuck with my sister, and no one ever went on to fuck with me either.  

Doing the right thing is hard sometimes for some folks, I’ve lived my life by the foundation of a little grace, not sugarcoat shit, and taking care of things probably in a unorthodox none-pussy footed mindset, and it’s always worked out well for me. 

This so why I treat scammers the way I do, because a majority of them are just pussies on a school bus who think it’s cute to make fun or take advantage of those who are not as educated as others, anytime I see a scam artist block me first, I always think of how lonely life must be to think on that wave length to take advantage of others.  

Just remember, if you scam people on this app, I will find you, I will expose you, I will report you, and I will eventually wear you so far fucking out, you’ll get tired of me. I will always throw punches for those who cannot stand up for themselves, in the last two weeks I’ve created a list of the running scammers, I’d like you to take some time out of your day. I’d like you to find that post…. And upvote it, bookmark it, and maybe even share it around. 

Today once enemies came together to “handle” the trash, once we as a collective group start taking out the trash together, we can focus on the good. 

Fight the good fight. 
And let’s clean up the feeds for the real TA and the real folks to chirp the good word of the market. 

Cheers to sweeping the sunshine under the shade sometimes.

One thing that really puts this into perspective is the odds of success in this space.

The financial content world is extremely competitive. Thousands of people start newsletters, Substacks, Discords, and research services every year, but only a small percentage ever build a meaningful audience, establish trust, and turn it into a sustainable business.

Most creators never make it past the early stage the stage where you are putting in countless hours with little recognition, few subscribers, and no guarantee that anyone is paying attention. The creators who succeed are usually the ones who stay consistent, continue improving, and provide real value long before the rewards show up.

That is why what you crafted with Hidden Gems Research stands out. You didn’t start with a massive audience or a guaranteed path to success. You started with knowledge, passion, and the commitment to keep showing up every single day.

The fact that you were willing to put in that work while it was still complimentary, while building trust around ONDAS and expanding the depth of your research, is what separates true builders from people who simply chase attention.

Success in this industry is earned, and the odds are not in most people’s favor. Building something people voluntarily subscribe to, trust, and follow is a major accomplishment.

🔔Citadel Securities’ Fed Rate Hike Call Adds to Market Angst
body:
(Bloomberg) -- On the eve of the Federal Reserve's policy decision, bond traders are on edge. While most expect policymakers to leave interest rates unchanged, prominent voices across Wall Street are putting their weight behind a hike in just the second meeting run by new Chairman Kevin Warsh.

It's indicative of a new regime at the Fed, with Warsh looking to diverge from his predecessors by no longer signaling interest-rate decisions to markets well in advance. A hike would establish Warsh's inflation-fighting credibility, leading some, like Citadel Securities and PGIM, to assign a higher chance of an increase Wednesday. For traders, it means greater angst, illustrated by the record demand seen this week to hedge against a surprise rate hike.

"Warsh is still kind of a wildcard, he's been pretty adamant that he's not interested in forward guidance," said Joe Boyle, fixed income investment specialist at Hartford Funds. "He's not interested in telegraphing anything but maybe something slips, maybe he does do something that's perceived as forward guidance."

As of 3:30 p.m. Tuesday in New York, swap-market pricing implied a roughly one-in-three chance that policymakers raise the key benchmark rate by 25 basis points, even as Treasuries headed for their longest gaining streak in a month.

The chorus in favor of the case for a rate hike is growing. In a surprise move, Frank Flight, the head of macro strategy at Citadel Securities, flipped his base case this week to an increase, in what he said "would emphatically end the forward guidance era" while underscoring the Fed's independence.

Wrightson ICAP's chief economist Lou Crandall said there is no good reason for the Fed not to raise interest rates. At PGIM, head of global bonds and chief investment strategist Robert Tipp said the market is probably underestimating the probability of a move Wednesday.

"He has really set the stage for a hike," Tipp said. "Putting off the decision now would raise the probability to do a 50 in September."

Bond market veteran Harley Bassman went a step further, arguing in a note Tuesday that the Fed should "rip off the band aid" and raise rates by half a point — a move that would both give it credibility on fighting inflation and fend off pressure from President Donald Trump to lower borrowing costs.

title: Leopold Aschenbrenner's Situational Awareness unwinds hedge fund with up to $24B after leveraged AI bets fail
body:
Leopold Aschenbrenner's hedge fund Situational Awareness has completely unwound its investment portfolio after suffering heavy losses on its AI and software trades, according to CNBC's David Faber. The fund sold its entire portfolio to another hedge fund as it worked to exit its positions. The hedge fund managed around $20 billion to $24 billion in assets before the unwind.

The fund came under pressure after losses from AI-related investments and short bets against software companies hurt its portfolio. Earlier, Bank of America, Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chase helped the fund manage its positions and meet margin requirements, according to earlier CNBC reporting citing people familiar with the discussions.
The banks also helped the fund reduce its positions in an orderly manner instead of forcing a rushed sell-off. Before Thursday's trading session, prime brokers were already marketing both the fund's long and short positions to potential buyers.
The fund also approached its existing investors and lenders to raise fresh capital as financial pressure increased. Situational Awareness additionally offered parts of its investment portfolio directly to some investors. One person familiar with those discussions said these efforts were "ad hoc rather than a coordinated fundraise," according to the Financial Times.
How the fund went from huge gains to heavy losses
Situational Awareness reported an impressive 439% net return through June 30, according to a July 24 investor letter. The strong returns were boosted by the fund's use of leverage, which amplified gains during the AI stock rally. However, the same leverage increased losses when AI-related stocks fell sharply in July.
CNBC reported that investments in AI infrastructure companies, including SK Hynix, lost value during the market decline. At the same time, the fund's short positions against software companies such as Adobe also moved against it. Several publicly disclosed holdings of the fund dropped more than 35% during July.
Those stocks included Nebius, SanDisk, Micron and CoreWeave. The wider technology market also weakened during the month, adding pressure on the fund's portfolio, according to the Financial Times. The Nasdaq 100 fell about 10% in July. South Korea's Kospi index also lost roughly one-third of its value during the same period.
Also read: Why Nvidia, Nebius, Amazon and AI stocks are rising today as Microsoft Azure growth boosts sector
The fund's massive options exposure
Situational Awareness's March 31 Form 13F showed it held $13.68 billion across 42 investments. Around $8.46 billion, or 62% of the portfolio's reported value, consisted of put-option exposure linked to semiconductor and technology stocks. The fund's biggest reported put-option position was $2.04 billion tied to the VanEck Semiconductor ETF.
Another major position was $1.57 billion tied to Nvidia. The reported values represented the value of the underlying securities, not the amount paid for the options, according to the filing. The filing did not disclose important details such as the options' strike prices, expiration dates, leverage used or offsetting positions. Because of those missing details, it is impossible to know whether the put options were bearish bets or simply hedges protecting the portfolio.
Anthropic stake put up for sale
The hedge fund also marketed its private-company investments, including its stake in Anthropic, according to CNBC. Potential buyers have shown interest in the Anthropic stake. However, the size of the proposed sale and the possible price have not been disclosed. Situational Awareness participated in Anthropic's Series H funding round in May.
That funding round valued Anthropic at $65 billion. After the funding round, Anthropic's post-money valuation reached $96.5 billion. Anthropic confidentially filed a draft registration statement on June 1.
In his July investor letter, Aschenbrenner said a possible Anthropic IPO could become a major catalyst during the second half of the year. The same investor letter also opened an August 1 subscription window for investors. In the letter, the technology stock sell-off was presented as an opportunity for investors to commit additional capital

title: Consumers are allergic to the high-interest-rate flu
body:
Low interest rates aren’t just cheaper money 
they’re rocket fuel for an economy

A family that would happily move into a bigger home at 3% suddenly sits on the sidelines at 6%. The same thing happens with cars. Boats. RVs. Home renovations. Small business expansion. People don’t stop wanting these things they stop pulling the trigger 

Activity breeds activity

One home sale creates another. Movers get hired. Contractors get work. Furniture gets bought. Appliances get replaced. Landscapers get called. Realtors, lenders, title companies, insurance agents, and retailers all eat from the same table

The same goes for cars. One new truck sold means trade-ins, financing, insurance, accessories, detailing, maintenance, and more money changing hands throughout the economy

Right now, millions of homeowners are sitting on mortgages around 3%. The current market is closer to 6%. That’s not just a higher payment it’s a psychological wall.

People want a new house

People want a new car

But doubling the cost of borrowing freezes movement

And when people stop moving, money stops moving.

The economy isn’t powered by dollars sitting still. It’s powered by confidence, transactions, and velocity.

Lower rates don’t create demand they unlock the demand that’s already there

That’s why interest rates don’t just influence the economy

They determine how fast it breathes

title: $VIX is lying to you…
body:
There’s a historic phenomenon where the market always looks calm before it breaks. And there’s a unique set up that’s happening right now….within the options market. 

In 1999 investors weren’t just buying the stock market they were buying a “theme” that theme was called the Internet. 

In that theme rose 86% on the Nasdaq. 
Cisco with the time was the one that was selling the hardware behind the big boom…. It was on pace to become one of the most valuable companies on the planet earth. 

But the average stock where was it going? No where. Only really a handful of names carried everything…. 

Here’s a really important part, underneath it all that’s where the options market started to split, volatility on single names like Cisco they started to get really really volatile and really expensive, but the index volatility on the S&P 500 in the NASDAQ stayed really cheap, if you want to visualize that, it just means that dispersion rose, to stock started to trade on their own storylines, so correlation started to fail stock stopped moving all together. 

Now if you what to throw this on the trading screen click pull it up and type in VIX EQ MINUS VIX 

Now everything was home along the Internet world, until the macro changed. The feds took rates to 6.5 percent and the cap ex behind the Internet was funded (we’re still in 1999 people) and the cap ex is funded like this today with debt. 

Then the math stopped working, stocks started moving
Together again, but this time it was on the way down, when the dust settled the Nasdaq was down 75 percent.  

Let’s swap fiber for gpus today ,and Cisco for micron, the same split in this volatility is happening right now… same name volume has been glorious, index volume is cheap, but the last month this is starting to reset, the ai stuff is down 25 percent,  so this volatility spread is normalizing… while rates stay high, and cap ex still keeps going. 

I think the main theme here is the market is losing control
Of it’s narrative, so when you see VIX on the screen and it seems cool and calm and collected, it doesn’t mean it’s the same thing as safe.

Current structure

Call Wall: 775
Net Gamma Regime: Positive Net GEX 5.3 Billion to 12.8 Billion

Baby First 

SPY is already operating in the volatility dampened, dip buying mode of net-positive gamma above 767 

However 775 represents the immediate structural hurdle (the Call Wall) that needs to be broken to trigger the next wave of forced dealer buying
￼

What SPY Is (and Isn't) Showing Right Now￼

1. SPY IS above the Gamma Flip (Net Positive Gamma)

Because SPY is trading above the 767 Gamma Flip level *dealers are in net-positive gamma territory* 

As described this causes dealers to buy dips and sell rips, which compresses implied volatility and turns price action into a steady, *mean reverting grind higher!*

2. SPY *is testing not yet past *the Call Wall
The major Call Wall sits at 775 

Here is how the mechanics differ at this structure of what is seen

title: A Timeline Into The Bears …..
body:
Over the past decade, market bears have repeatedly called for catastrophic crashes or prolonged stagnation, only for markets to break record high after record high.  

1. The Post-Brexit & 2016 Trump Election "Doom Calls" (2016)
 The Bear Argument: Wall Street analysts and macro bears widely predicted that if the UK voted for Brexit or if Donald Trump won the U.S. presidential election, global equity markets would immediately plunge into a multi-year bear market.
 What Actually Happened: Following a brief overnight futures panic after the election, the stock market launched into a massive, multi-year rally (the "Trump Rally"), leading to double-digit gains for major indexes in 2016 and 2017.

2. The "Guaranteed Slowdown" of 2017
 The Bear Argument: Prominent bears argued that after eight straight years of a bull market since the 2008 financial crisis, stock valuations were ridiculously stretched and overdue for a major 30%–50% correction.
 What Actually Happened: 2017 ended up being one of the calmest, most relentless bull market years in history. The S&P 500 did not experience a single 3% pull-back all year, posting a gain of over 19%.

3. The 2019 "Fed Rate Hike Recession"
 The Bear Argument: After the Fed raised interest rates in late 2018 (causing a sharp 19.8% Q4 dip), bears argued that the business cycle had officially ended, calling for an unavoidable recession in 2019.  
 What Actually Happened: The Fed paused and subsequently cut rates, leading to a massive rebound. The S&P 500 surged over 31% in 2019, making it one of the best single-year returns of the century.

4. Calling for "Great Depression II" During the March 2020 COVID Bottom
 The Bear Argument: As global economies shut down during the onset of COVID-19 and the S&P 500 plummeted 34% in a single month, high-profile bears warned that stocks would stay suppressed for years due to supply chain collapses and mass unemployment.  
 What Actually Happened: Driven by historic monetary stimulus, tech transformation, and retail liquidity, the market hit new all-time highs just 5 months later, delivering the fastest bear-market recovery in recorded history.

5. The "Guaranteed 2023 Recession" Consensus
 The Bear Argument: Following the brutal 2022 inflationary bear market (where the S&P fell ~25% and tech stocks cratered), over 80% of Wall Street economists predicted a guaranteed U.S. recession in 2023 as the Fed hiked rates past 5%.  
 What Actually Happened: The U.S. economy avoided a recession entirely ("the soft landing"), and the S&P 500 roared back with a ~24% gain in 2023, largely catalyzed by the generative AI boom.  

6. The 2024 "Higher for Longer Will Break Everything" Fear
 The Bear Argument: Bears insisted that sticky inflation and interest rates staying at 20-year highs throughout 2024 would choke corporate earnings, force commercial real estate bankruptcies, and cause tech stocks to collapse under high valuation multiples.
 What Actually Happened: Corporate earnings beat expectations, mega-cap tech expanded profitability, and major indexes repeatedly touched record highs through 2024.

7. The Persistent "AI Bubble Burst" & Tariff Warnings (2025–2026)
 The Bear Argument: Critics drawn parallel between the modern AI software surge and the 1999 Dot-Com bubble, predicting a major collapse as trade friction and tariff disputes spiked volatility.  
 What Actually Happened: While the market experienced sharp pullback windows (such as mid-2025 trade volatility), corporate capital spending in hardware and productivity kept underlying earnings strong, allowing markets to consistently absorb corrections and push higher.

The Cost of Being a Bear: Sitting in cash, buying put options, or shorting stocks incurs heavy costs over time cash loses value to inflation, options expire worthless, and short positions face unlimited downside risk while paying interest to borrow shares. Wall Street has a famous saying: "Permabears have predicted 20 out of the last 2 recessions.

title: OPEX Week and No War Deal …..
body:
Think of the market like a rubber band stretched over a bunch of magnets

During normal weeks, the rubber band moves around fairly normally

During OPEX week, there are HUGE amounts of options expiring. Those options create magnets around certain SPX/SPY - QQQ prices. Market makers are constantly adjusting their hedges, which can pull price toward important strike or cause violent moves away from them.

Now add geopolitical uncertainly 

If headlines say:

Peace talks are progressing

Stocks can rip higher

Then

No agreement reached

Stocks can suddenly dump

And because there are so many options expiring, that move can get amplified

The biggest things I’d watch

1. Don’t trust the first move

OPEX loves fakeouts

SPX breaks yesterday’s high …. everyone buys calls ….market reverses

SPX breaks yesterday’s low ….everyone buys puts …..market rips back up.

The first move isn’t necessarily the real move

2. Geopolitical headlines can overpower technicals.

If a major Russia/Ukraine headline hits while you’re sitting in a 0DTE SPX trade, your beautiful support/resistance setup can become irrelevant for a few minutes

That’s why I’d be especially careful holding contracts through headline risk.

3. Watch the big strikes

Think of major strikes as magnets

If SPX keeps getting pulled toward a major level and can’t escape it, don’t keep buying calls and puts expecting a huge move.

Sometimes the market’s answer is simply

We’re staying right here until these options expire.

4. 0DTE can make you feel like you’re right when you’re actually losing

You buy a call

SPX moves slightly in your direction

You think

YES! I’m right!

But SPX stalls for 10 minutes

Your option gets destroyed by theta.

You were directionally right and still lost money

5. Wait for confirmation

During OPEX, I’d rather miss the first 10 points than jump into a fake breakout and lose 30

Look for

Level breaks ….volume confirms …price holds the level ….THEN enter.

And here’s the big picture

OPEX low summer liquidity ….geopolitical uncertainty potentially nasty price action 

You can get huge candles, reversals, fake breakouts and extremely fast 0DTE premium changes

So this isn’t necessarily a week to say:

I’m going to make 10 trades today

It’s more like

I’m going to wait for the market to show me what it’s doing, then attack the clean setups 

- HOPE THIS HELPS SAVE YOU HEARTACHE

Volume 101
body:
Think of the market like a school cafeteria

Price tells you what happened

Volume tells you how many people actually cared

That is why volume is one of the most important metrics in the market

Imagine SPY is sitting at 640 dollars

It moves to 642 dollars

Sounds bullish right

Not necessarily

If SPY went from 640 to 642 on massive volume that tells you a lot of traders and institutions were involved in that move

But if it went from 640 to 642 on very light volume you have to be more skeptical

It could simply be a lack of sellers

Price tells you where the market moved

Volume tells you how much participation was behind the move

Think of volume like attendance at school

If 20 people show up to class and the teacher says we are having a vote that vote does not mean much

If 2000 people show up suddenly that vote carries a lot more weight

The market works similarly

Low volume means fewer participants and moves can be easier to push around

High volume means more participation and moves generally have more conviction behind them

That is why summer trading can be deceptive

You can see SPY ripping higher and think the market is incredibly bullish

Meanwhile half of Wall Street is on vacation

Then you have the Greeks

Delta tells you how much your option reacts to a move in the stock

Gamma tells you how quickly that Delta changes

Think of Delta as your speed and Gamma as your acceleration

Theta is time decay

Every day that passes your option generally loses some value simply because you are running out of time

Theta is basically the market charging you rent for holding the option

Vega tells you how much your option reacts to changes in implied volatility

If traders suddenly become terrified and start paying huge premiums for protection volatility can explode and Vega becomes very important

Now put the Greeks and volume together

Price going up with volume going up gives you stronger confirmation that buyers are participating

Price going up with volume going down means you need to be careful because the market is moving but participation is not necessarily following

Price going down with volume going up tells you selling pressure has real participation behind it

Price going down with volume going down could simply mean there is a lack of buyers rather than aggressive selling

Volume does not predict the market

It gives you context

And this is where I am watching August

We are starting to see volume creep back in as we approach the end of August

That is important

We have spent a lot of the summer dealing with lighter liquidity and vacation season participation

As traders come back volume can start increasing

When volume comes back moves can become more meaningful in both directions

But here is the Freeballer warning

Do not confuse returning volume with automatically returning bullishness

More volume simply means more players are back at the table

Now we get to see what those players actually want to do

Watch the price and volume combination rather than price by itself

Because the market can lie to you with price

Volume is the attendance sheet

And as August winds down I am watching that attendance sheet very closely

title: Thoughts on the Clarity Act
body:
*The CLARITY Act is genuinely in trouble. The Senate punted it into September, and Reuters reports that it faces a difficult path because it needs 60 votes and there are disagreements over ethics, AML protections and stablecoin provisions*

TD Cowen’s Washington Research Group currently puts the odds of it becoming law in the next few months at only 25%. 

At the same time, the Trump administration is moving ahead with crypto regulation without Congress, through the SEC and CFTC. Reuters specifically says the agencies are advancing their own crypto framework while the legislation stalls. 
 
 
And here’s the really interesting part: Wall Street is already positioning around tokenization regardless of whether CLARITY passes. BlackRock, Fidelity, Franklin Templeton, Goldman Sachs and SoFi have publicly backed the bill. 

*There is actually evidence for part of this broader rotation thesis: the SEC is working on exemptions and frameworks for tokenized assets even while CLARITY is stuck in Congress*

The biggest rotation of our generation?
body:
Capital is increasingly moving away from long-duration sovereign bonds while simultaneously chasing equities, crypto, gold, commodities and other scarce/risk assets even as the cost of capital is rising.

That combination is what deserves attention.

What is happening right now

1. The bond market is sending the biggest warning.

The 30-year Treasury yield hit about 5.34% during the recent selloff — its highest level since 2007 while the 10-year has been around 4.7%. 

That’s extremely important because normally you would expect stocks to have a much harder time when long-term yields are moving this high.

Instead, equities have remained remarkably resilient. As of August 20, the S&P 500 was still up 11.6% YTD, Nasdaq 12.2%, and Russell 2000 20.6%.

So we’re seeing

Higher long-term rates + strong stocks + exploding crypto + strong gold.

That’s the weird part.

⸻

2. Crypto is now absorbing institutional capital at a scale that didn’t exist in previous cycles.

This isn’t simply retail traders buying Bitcoin.

Between August 17–21, U.S. spot Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs reportedly took in roughly $2.62 billion in one week, their strongest weekly performance of 2026. 

Bitcoin ETFs alone had a roughly $517 million net-inflow day on August 20. 

And Bitcoin subsequently surged more than 20% in the week, approaching $80,000. 

That matters because ETFs have effectively turned crypto into another institutional asset-allocation bucket.

It’s no longer:

“Should I buy some Bitcoin?”

It’s increasingly:

“What percentage of the portfolio belongs in digital assets?”

That’s a structural change.

But here’s where I think your idea gets REALLY interesting

I don’t think the best description is:

Stocks → Crypto

I think it’s closer to:

Bonds → risk assets + scarce assets

Think about the four big buckets:￼

Asset

What is happening

Treasuries

Investors demanding higher yields

Stocks

Still attracting enormous capital

Bitcoin/crypto

Institutional inflows accelerating

Gold

Strong demand / record territory

That’s unusual.

And there’s a common denominator:

Investors increasingly don’t want to hold long-duration government debt at today’s fiscal/inflation risk.

The U.S. government’s debt is now above $40 trillion, while deficits and enormous government borrowing are increasing the amount of debt the market has to absorb. At the same time, companies — particularly AI/data-center companies — are issuing huge amounts of debt. 

That means the bond market has a supply problem.

Investors are basically saying:

“If you’re going to lend the government money for 20–30 years, I want to be paid.”

Hence the 5%+ 30-year yield.



And then something REALLY unusual happened

On August 19, Treasury announced that it would double its long-term Treasury buybacks to at least $4 billion per operation.

Stocks, bonds, gold and Bitcoin all rallied. 

That is fascinating.

Why?

Because Treasury basically gave the market a signal:

“We’re willing to actively improve liquidity in the long end of the Treasury market.”

And markets immediately interpreted that as supportive for financial assets.

Bitcoin reacted particularly violently.

That’s why I wouldn’t dismiss the idea that liquidity is becoming the dominant force.


The Fed situation makes this even stranger

The Fed’s balance sheet isn’t exploding like it did during COVID.

In fact, the latest Federal Reserve data show roughly $6.47 trillion of securities held outright, while reserve balances were around $2.94 trillion as of August 19. 

So this isn’t simply:

“The Fed printed trillions and everything went up.”

Instead, we’re getting liquidity from several different places:

* government fiscal spending
* Treasury debt issuance
* Treasury buybacks
* corporate borrowing
* institutional ETF flows
* money-market liquidity
* private credit
* retail participation
* international capital

That’s much more complicated than a traditional QE-driven bull market.

⸻

And this is where I would NOT call it unprecedented

We’ve seen pieces of this before.

1999–2000

Technology stocks exploded while traditional valuation metrics became increasingly irrelevant.

2006–2007

Stocks remained strong while cracks were developing in credit and housing.

2020–2021

We had perhaps the clearest example of:

stocks + crypto + commodities + speculative assets all exploding simultaneously.

But that was accompanied by extraordinary monetary stimulus.

2026 is different.

We’re getting something more like:

strong equities + explosive crypto + strong gold + weak long-duration bonds + high government borrowing + elevated inflation risk.

That particular combination is much less common.

So I wouldn’t say:

“We’ve never seen anything like this.”

I’d say:

“The current combination is historically unusual, particularly because risk assets are performing strongly while the long end of the world’s largest bond market is under significant pressure.”

That’s a much stronger argument.

⸻

Here’s the part I’d watch VERY closely

There are essentially two possible futures from here.

🟢 Scenario 1 — The liquidity supercycle continues

This is the bullish scenario.

Treasury successfully stabilizes the bond market.

Long-term yields stop climbing.

The Fed eventually becomes more accommodative.

The dollar weakens.

ETF flows continue.

AI earnings remain strong.

Capital continues migrating toward:

stocks → crypto → gold → commodities → emerging markets

Under this scenario, Bitcoin could become one of the biggest beneficiaries because it’s one of the most liquidity-sensitive assets.

One research analysis found a very strong historical relationship between Bitcoin and global liquidity, although the exact relationship shouldn’t be treated as a reliable forecasting formula. 

If this scenario develops, 2026–27 could become a major risk-asset expansion phase.

⸻

🔴 Scenario 2 — The bond market eventually wins

This is the dangerous scenario.

Imagine:

10-year → 5%+

30-year → 6%+

Inflation remains sticky.

Oil stays elevated.

Government deficits remain enormous.

The Fed can’t cut.

Treasury has to keep issuing enormous amounts of debt.

Eventually investors say:

“I’m not buying risk assets when I can get 6% from the government.”

Then the capital flow reverses.

And that’s where you’d potentially see:

Bonds ↑ yields
Stocks ↓
Crypto ↓↓↓
Dollar ↑
Volatility ↑

Crypto would probably be hit hardest because it’s the highest-beta liquidity asset.

And here’s the indicator I’d personally watch

Forget trying to predict whether SPX goes up tomorrow.

I’d watch these five things together:

① 10-year Treasury

If it breaks decisively higher, that’s a problem.

② 30-year Treasury

This might actually be the most important chart in the entire market right now.

5.3% is already historically significant.

③ Bitcoin ETF flows

If Bitcoin continues getting hundreds of millions/billions of institutional inflows even while yields remain elevated, that’s evidence of a genuine structural shift.

④ Dollar

A falling dollar alongside rising BTC/gold/equities would strengthen the “capital seeking alternatives to U.S. fixed income/currency” thesis.

⑤ S&P 500 breadth

If SPX continues rising but fewer and fewer stocks participate, that’s a warning.

⸻

My bigger-picture read

I wouldn’t call this the beginning of a stock-market collapse.

Actually, the data currently suggest something more interesting:

We’re potentially entering a period where the market is repricing what “safe” actually means.

For decades:

Cash → Treasuries → stocks → speculative assets

was the traditional risk ladder.

But if investors become increasingly concerned about:

* government debt
* inflation
* currency debasement
* fiscal deficits
* geopolitical risk
* long-duration bonds

then the hierarchy starts changing.

You could end up with:

Cash → short-duration instruments → productive assets → gold → Bitcoin → speculative assets

while long-duration government bonds become less attractive.

That’s a major structural shift, if it persists.

And the fact that Bitcoin, gold and equities can rally while long-duration Treasuries are getting hammered is the part I’d take seriously.

*The bond market is arguably the most important signal in the entire setup right now, not Bitcoin.*

title: September Is Here
body:
And every year the same shit happens

People look at the calendar, see September, see “historically the worst month,” see red candles, and immediately start screaming:

“THE MARKET IS FUCKED.”

Relax

September is historically ugly. Since 1928, the S&P 500 has averaged roughly a -1.1% to -1.2% September return, with September producing more down months than any other month

The Nasdaq has historically averaged around -0.8%. (The Wall Street Journal⁠￼)

But here’s the part people conveniently forget

Historical weakness does NOT mean automatic collapse

The market can absolutely rip higher in September

And 2026 has another variable sitting directly on top of all of this 


TRUMP + THE MIDTERMS

We’re entering a period where policy, tariffs, taxes, regulation, interest rates, government spending, geopolitical headlines and election positioning can all move markets

And the market doesn’t give a shit about your political opinion

It cares about earnings, liquidity, rates, inflation, positioning and expectations

The 2026 midterms make the next few months especially interesting

Historically, midterm years can be choppy heading into Election Day, but the historical pattern AFTER the election is a completely different story

Since 1974, the S&P 500 has averaged roughly +5.7% in the three months following midterm elections, with 11 of 13 periods positive

Six months after the midterms?

+12.4% average


All 13 historical periods were positive.
(Schwab Brokerage⁠￼)

That’s why I’m not interested in the

“September = crash”

narrative.

I’m interested in what the market actually does.

Watch SPX

Watch volume

Watch breadth

Watch whether dips are being bought or sold

Watch whether major support levels are defended

Watch whether new highs are being confirmed by participation or whether the index is being held up by a handful of mega caps

Because here’s the thing

PRICE TELLS YOU WHAT IS HAPPENING.
VOLUME TELLS YOU HOW MUCH PARTICIPATION IS BEHIND IT

Low-volume weakness isn’t necessarily the same thing as institutional distribution

And lower volume strength isn’t necessarily the same thing as a healthy breakout

You want to see confirmation!!!!

If SPX breaks support with expanding volume, breadth deteriorates and volatility starts expanding?

Pay attention to that area right there. 

If SPX sells off, volume stays relatively contained, sellers fail to follow through and buyers step in at important levels?

That’s a completely different fucking market.

And don’t forget the other side of September

October exists

Then November

Then December

Historically, November through April has been the strongest six-month stretch for stocks. (Fidelity⁠)

So a September pullback isn’t automatically the beginning of the end

Sometimes it’s simply the market resetting positioning before the next leg

We’ve seen this movie before

Corrections feel enormous while you’re standing inside them

Years later, they’re often just a fucking dent on the chart.

Since 1980, the S&P 500 has experienced an average peak-to-trough decline of roughly 14% during a calendar year, yet the average calendar-year return has still been about 13.3%. (Fidelity⁠)

Read that again

A market can drop 10–15% during the year and STILL finish the year meaningfully higher

That’s the entire fucking game.

You don’t need every candle to be green

You need to survive the red ones

September could be ugly

Trump can create volatility

The midterms can create uncertainty

The Fed can change the narrative overnight

Rates can rip

Oil can rip

SPX can dump 100 points and have everyone convinced the world is ending

None of that automatically means the bull thesis is dead

The wildcard isn’t predicting exactly what happens

The wildcard is how the market reacts when it happens

That’s what I’m watching

Not fear

Not headlines

The scammers, spam accounts, impersonators, and Telegram scams aren’t going to stop because we complain about them. If the platform isn’t able to solve the problem by itself, then we as a community need to come together and build something that helps protect each other.

Last week, we came together and showed just how much we care about AfterHour and the community we’ve built here.

Now I want to go one step further.

I’m putting together a Fraud Prevention & Community Safety Team, and I’m looking for people who want to help build something legitimate and useful.

🛡️ What we’re going to discuss Sunday:

• Fraud-prevention website building a centralized resource for identifying and reporting scams.

• Community outreach & support helping educate members about common scams, impersonation, phishing, fake trading groups, Telegram scams, etc.

• Custom documentation/reporting system creating a secure link where people can submit screenshots, usernames, Telegram handles, scam messages, and other documentation that can be organized and shared appropriately.

• Ideas for AfterHour — developing practical recommendations for how the platform could better identify and prevent repeat scammers and spam accounts.

• Community safety committee — establishing a group of committed members who can help identify trends, organize reports, and assist the community.

👨‍💻 WHO I’M LOOKING FOR

I specifically need:

• Programmers / developers
• Website builders
• Cybersecurity / fraud-prevention minded people
• Community moderators
• People willing to serve on the Safety Committee
• And honestly, anyone who has a good idea

You don’t have to be a programmer to contribute.

If you have an idea that could make AfterHour safer, I want to hear it.

We’re not going to harass people, dox anyone, hack anyone, or play vigilante.

We’re going to document, educate, organize, and report.

The goal is simple:

Make it harder for scammers to operate and easier for legitimate members to recognize and report them.

I’m not doing this to make money.

If we’re going to save this community, we have to do it together.

title: 🔑 Points Worth Remembering This Week As You Trade
body:
1. CPI Friday  (probably the biggest immediate risk)

A hotter-than-expected CPI could push yields higher and increase expectations for Fed tightening. That combination is bad for high-beta tech and especially dangerous for leveraged/0DTE longs. 

2. 10-year yield  watch (4.8–5%)
If yields continue climbing while SPX is falling, that’s a much more concerning signal than SPX simply having a red day. 

The 10-year has already reached roughly 4.81%!

3. Oil staying above $100
This is a nasty combination: higher oil /inflation fears /higher yields /less room for the Fed to ease Brent has now pushed above $100

4. VIX breaking out
VIX around 15–16 isn’t panic. I’d become considerably more defensive if you start seeing 18 /20+ while SPX is simultaneously losing support. VIX jumped about 8% Tuesday but remains below 20 

5. Market breadth
Don’t just watch SPX If SPX is flat but

* fewer stocks participate in rallies
* Nasdaq breadth deteriorates
* semiconductors start leading lower
* SPY closes near its lows

*that’s a warning that the index is being held up by a handful of names*

Oh and Next week 30% of ALL options expire in the market. The largest ever in the history of history’s of history of the market. That’s next Friday. According to JP Morgan Bank. 

The HISTORY of ALL HISTORIES. Now that doesn’t mean that the market is gonna crash or anything like that. It just means that the room for expansion is well… 🤷‍♂️
